items.body:
Swedish jazz icon Christer Bothén returns to Black Truffle backed by Ghosted's Oren Ambarchi, Johan Berthling and Andreas Werliin, playing bass clarinet and donso n’goni over the trio's signature kraut-jazz grooves. Hypnotic, trance-inducing biz FFO Natural Information Society, Don Cherry's 'Organic Music Society', Jon Hassell, The Necks.

If you're up on your Swedish jazz, there's no way you won't have stumbled across multi-instrumentalist Bothén. He's still best known for palling around with Don Cherry when the jazz great moved to Scandinavia, even teaching him how to play the donso n'goni, a sacred "hunter's harp" from the Wassoulou region in West Africa that Bothén had picked up when he was in Mali. And he's continued to perform with various local artists and outfits, conspicuously appearing on Ghosted's 2022 debut album just mere moments before Ambarchi's Black Truffle imprint re-issued his lost Afro-fusion classic album 'Trancedance'. Last year, Bothén finally issued his first solo n'goni album and now he's back on Black Truffle with this fleshed-out collaboration with the Ghosted crew, leading Ambarchi's Leslie-cab guitar drones, Berthling's bass and Werliin's drums.

Berthling and Werliin take the lead at first on the title track, hammering out a rotating groove before Bothén lets rip on bass clarinet. And playing a side role, Ambarchi might have the most important presence, using his signature phased, organ-like tones to provide anchoring drones for Bothén's spirited improvisations. He's even more pivotal on 'Antigorite', playing cascading staccato notes over those Leslie moans and creating an rhythmelodic foil for the other three players' more traditional interplay. But it's when Bothén plays the n'ghoni that the album really hits its stride; on 'Lizardite', those buzzing tones offset Ambarchi's crystalline twangs, filling in for Werliin's imposing basslines. It's the moment where everything else just drops into place, creating a structural crescendo before the album careers into darkness on the brilliantly moody closer 'Chrysotile'.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是瑞典爵士老将Christer Bothén与Ghosted乐队（Oren Ambarchi、Johan Berthling、Andreas Werliin）在Black Truffle厂牌下的合作。Bothén横跨低音单簧管与西非唐索恩贡尼琴（猎人竖琴），与三位搭档展开自由即兴对话。Ambarchi以Leslie喇叭效果的吉他持续音铺设稳定背景，Berthling的低音与Werliin的鼓构成循环往复的律动骨架，而Bothén的演奏从浑厚单簧管到嗡鸣的恩贡尼琴，为整体增添灵性色彩与非洲传统底蕴。专辑呈现出冥想式、催眠式的氛围，从开局的律动铺垫到恩贡尼琴主导段落的结构渐强，最终收束于阴郁的终曲，层次分明且叙事感强烈。评论将其与Natural Information Society、Don Cherry的《Organic Music Society》及Jon Hassell等先驱并列，凸显其在kraut-jazz与Afro-fusion交叉领域的独特位置。

items.body:
Our Darkness descends upon Dark Entries with a reissue of Anne Clark’s epochal proto-house masterpiece from 1984.

"As a young poet, Clark found herself drawn to London’s emerging punk scene. She became acquainted with Psychic TV affiliate David Harrow, with whom she would collaborate on 1983’s Changing Places and 1984’s Joined Up Writing. “Our Darkness,” off the latter album, was released as a single on Ink Records that same year, and became an underground club hit. It’s a singular piece of music: Clark’s lyrics, delivered with equal parts muscular confidence and unease, speak of urban alienation and heartbreak, while Harrow’s production pummels the listener with hydraulic beats and gloom-laced arpeggios. The song’s spirit would prove influential on both the early Chicago house and Detroit techno scenes, where mechanistic funk and existential despair could catalyse dancefloor mayhem.

This reissue offers three versions of “Our Darkness”: the original 12” remix, the Razormaid mix, and a previously unreleased dub version uncovered by David Harrow. Also included is the extended mix of “Sleeper in Metropolis,” another dancefloor hit of Clark’s, as well as the elegiac “Poem for a Nuclear Romance.”

“Our Darkness” channels timeless longing and contemporary dismay, a classic overdue for a little light shed upon it."
items._cn_summary: Anne Clark 1984年专辑《Our Darkness》由独立厂牌 Dark Entries 再版发行，收录原版12寸混音、Razormaid混音以及此前未公开的Dub版本，附带延伸版《Sleeper in Metropolis》及沉思之作《Poem for a Nuclear Romance》。Clark以诗歌为底色的歌词探讨都市异化与心碎情绪，David Harrow的编曲以液压般的节奏与阴郁琶音构建声响骨架。作品融合了诗歌朗诵与电子节拍，将文学性引入舞曲领域，对早期芝加哥浩室与底特律 techno 场景产生深远影响。再版挖掘出此前未释出的Dub版本，为这张具有里程碑意义的地下俱乐部经典提供了新的聆听维度。整体制作兼具机械感的律动与存在主义式的绝望，在抒情与电子之间寻找独特平衡。

items.body:
Harking back to the vertiginous ambient sound of 2007's 'Language Barrier', Jeff McIlwain references Steve Reich and Susumu Yokota on his tenth album - his most cinematic, emotional project yet.

It makes sense somehow that after penning the poppy 'Long Light', McIlwain needed to walk in the opposite direction. Because the Lusine project has never just been one thing; since its beginnings in the late '90s, McIlwain has used the name to release choppy IDM, sturdy trip-hop, reductionist techno and placid ambient biz. Like 'Language Barrier', 'Melting Days' developed from film score work, and you can almost see the visuals on opener 'Sightline'. McIlwain uses the word "ambient" carefully; sure, the music is pegged to its washing, slow-motion pad sounds and submerged, brassy drones, but it's not entirely beatless. Here, McIlwain lets a molasses slow, almost inaudible kick do most of the heavy lifting, while a double-time click stands in for the hi-hat. On 'Bird's Eye', meanwhile, metallic hits flutter around the eroded central rhythm while McIlwain muffles his pads in the deep background.

He builds momentum on 'Pendulum' by waking up his deep, dubby soundscape with womping subs and wintery hits and on 'Intruder' curves the remnants of a voice around a skeletal, glitchy beat. McIlwain's idea of ambient music is open and all encompassing - it still belongs in the back room, but it's not just wallpaper.
items._cn_summary: 这是Lusine第十张专辑，从电影配乐工作中发展而来，延续了2007年《Language Barrier》的氛围路线，被认为是McIlwain最具电影感和情感深度的作品。制作上参考了Steve Reich的极简手法和Susumu Yokota的细腻质感。专辑并未走纯beatless路线，而是在缓慢的洗涤式pad音景中嵌入近乎听不见的底鼓和双倍速的click声响，金属打击在侵蚀的核心节奏周围闪烁。'Pendulum'中低频sub与寒冬般的打击唤醒dub感声场，'Intruder'则将人声残片缠绕在骨骼状的glitch节拍上。McIlwain对氛围音乐的理解是开放且包容的——它仍属于背景空间，但绝不只是壁纸，而是拥有自身呼吸与情绪重量的声音建筑。

items.body:
Picking up where 2024's 'Trash Can Lamb' left off, Keith Freund blurs the line between acoustic instrumentation and DIY electronics on his latest full-length, unraveling his gentle, jazzy sessions with 8-bit beats and oddball FX.

Since the beginning, Freund has been fixated on the character of a sound rather than what that sound, on its own, might represent. His piano parts rarely come off as if they've been played by hand; after chopping them to shreds, he inevitably reconstitutes them into player-piano style impossible sequences, re-organizing the notes and re-sculpting the tone completely. On 'Over Sidewalk Bryum', for example, it's the piano that provides the track's rhythm, accented by radio interference and bit-crushed oscillations. And although Freund does less chipping at his horn parts, letting the sax soar over the chattering electronics, it's still subtly tweaked - nothing's ever quite what it seems.

A swamp of discarded blips and glitches help prop up 'I'll Find a Place for Us', and Freund's soft woodwind tones make their way through the noise initially - or at least that's what we're supposed to think. In time, Freund's sax emerges and the soft-hued, woodwind-like sound is revealed to be a red herring. But that's the kind of sleight of hand that Freund seems to revel in, creating glitchy, unstable music from soft, placid sound sources, not the harsh digital detritus you'd expect to find on a Mille Plateaux disc.
items._genre: experimental jazz / DIY electronics / glitch / acoustic-electronic fusion
items._cn_summary: Keith Freund延续前作路线，将原声乐器演奏与DIY电子手法深度融合。钢琴片段被切碎重组为自动钢琴式的不可能序列，重塑音色与节奏结构；萨克斯与木管音色则穿梭于8-bit节拍、位元压缩振荡与无线电干扰之中。整张专辑的核心手法是从柔和、静态的声音素材出发，制造出不稳定的故障感与数字噪音纹理，与Mille Plateaux等厂牌的硬核数字残骸形成鲜明对比。Freund擅长在听感上设置听觉陷阱，例如看似木管的柔美音色实为电子伪装的声学误导。这种将爵士即兴的抒情性拆解并嫁接电子失稳逻辑的做法，呈现出鲜明的个人美学与声音设计意识，适合对实验爵士与电子交汇地带感兴趣的听众。

items.body:
Returning to Jabu's do you have peace? imprint, Bristol-based Ukrainian artist Regina Collage reflects on global and personal instability, infusing her haunted, lo-fi songs with tentative passion. It's gorgeous, fragile and deeply personal pop - somewhere between HTRK, Broadcast and Cukor Bila Smert’.

Hailing from Kharkiv where her parents still live, Collage is acutely aware of the lasting impacts of war - the severed relationships, the daily, ongoing trauma. In Bristol, she's away from the front line, but carries it with her, a feeling of "quiet shame" that grounds her latest album's subtle, minimal arrangements. Because although her voice is at the centre of the album, she rarely raises it to more than a distant whisper, sounding as if she's trapped in a liminal space between realities. On 'It Should Be Something', she drowns her moans in reverb, harmonising with echo trails, bass guitar plucks and languid riffs; it's music that won't come as a complete surprise to anyone familiar with Jabu's output, but Collage's outlook is slower, sadder and more exposed. Sure, she plays fast and loose with effects, but the processes never obscure the album's core emotions - heart-melting feelings we haven't heard rendered quite so perfectly since we locked in with Jonnine's 'Southside Girl'. 

'Horizont' is rooted in a kind of bedroom-recorded post-punk that's so slow and gummed up with noise you'd think it was some STROOM-related archival discovery. On 'Davno', her voice seems to float around a simple, distorted drum machine and ebbing analog synths, molded into casual moans that betray Collage's sobering, vulnerable themes. But she's almost in a different headspace altogether on 'I Hope', curling her words around a Hooky-style staccato bassline and anticipating a beat that never actually comes. Each song sounds as if it's a torn page from her scrapbook, not exactly half-finished, but certainly not polished - and it's this aesthetic that gives the album so much emotional weight. We get to reach into Collage's psyche, hearing her own instability as she wonders about a world that's been thrown into chaos. As she reconciles with the situation, figuring out her life in Bristol at the same time, she constructs a sound that's similarly dualistic - unashamedly displaying its roots in the Ukrainian underground while absorbing ideas from her new home.
items._cn_summary: 乌克兰艺术家 Regina Collage 来自哈尔科夫，现居布里斯托尔，这张专辑是她对战争背景下个人与全球动荡的沉思。整张作品以卧室录制的低保真方式呈现，合成器嗡鸣、失真鼓机与缓慢的贝斯线条交织，人声始终保持在近乎耳语的微弱音量，仿佛悬浮在现实的缝隙之中。她将乌克兰地下的粗糙质感与英国新家园的氛围相融合，歌曲结构呈现出一种未完成的手稿感——撕裂的页面、残缺的片段——恰恰是这种粗糙美学承载了专辑的情感重量。回声尾迹、慵懒的吉他拨弦与忧伤的呻吟融为一体，既私密又疏离。从与 Jabu 厂牌的关联到 HTRK、Broadcast 等参照系，作品在暗潮与低保真之间找到了独属于自己的平衡点，折射出流离者的内心地理。

items.body:
On Kirk Barley’s definitive solo gem, alternative tunings and a tactile feel for pitching rhythms generate their gentlest and most absorbing work, twinkling amid a microcosm of similar, exploratory productions from Mark Fell & Rian Treanor thru to Aleksi Perälä, Beatrice Dillon, Terry Riley & Jon Hassell.

Building on a decade of work spanning cuts for Brownswood thru to jams with Matthew Herbert and Matt Davies, ‘Arc’ finds Yorkshire-bred artist Barley fully indulge formative passions for microtonal just intonation - as seeded in Terry Riley’s ‘Shri Camel’ - and slippery syncopation to the fullest. Half solo, proper, and half peppered with percussion by regular spar, Matt Davies, it follows his nose for open frontiers of alternative tunings and wonky meter with the blend of low key modesty and prism-pushing tekkerz that have long endeared his work to lovers of lower case experimental music. 

Sweetly balanced between timeless, folk-soul-wise and futurist sensibilities, the half hour suite knits hyaline synths and rippling gamelan metallophonics with clarinet and guitar in lissom, sloshing shapes that effortlessly seduce, rather than demand, the listener’s attention. In particular we are drawn to the bits in duo with Davies, floating sublime ideas in the dreamlike, inverted dub architexture of ‘Ion’, settling on mind like a strangely bucolic Incus work on ’Sundry’, and thru the exquisite, tip-toed rhythms of ‘Ecstatic’, to a trippier, bittersweet type of ante-chamber music on ‘Fret (Hear)’.

He’s also deeply charming when left to his own devices. Ambient opener ‘Billow’ calls to mind the tenderness of Cotton Goods works, and ‘Knead’ chases a certain geist of Irdial or Plaid-esque gamelantronica into the sublime title tune, while ‘Prism’ most beautifully ties all his interests in a melting dream sequence which he caps with the harmonic nightlight glow of ‘Column’.
items._cn_summary: Kirk Barley的专辑《Arc》展现了他对微分音律（microtonal just intonation）的深度探索，这一灵感源自Terry Riley的《Shri Camel》。专辑融合另类调弦体系与滑溜的切分节奏，在低限实验音乐的脉络中开辟出独特的声响空间。制作上采用透明合成器音色与加美兰金属质感音效交织，配合单簧管与吉他的灵动编排，营造出既具民间灵魂气质又充满未来感的聆听体验。Matt Davies的打击乐加入为部分曲目增添了梦境般的倒置dub结构。专辑横跨纯粹氛围段落与节奏驱动的复合形态，如《Ion》《Ecstatic》《Prism》等曲目呈现从极简到复杂的渐变层次。整张作品以半小时的组曲形式，在低调内敛中展现了丰富的实验维度与声响层次。

items.body:
Not the birth of acid house, but a thrilling piece of synth raga set to brisk disco beats, Bollywood soundtrack composer Charanjit Singh’s ’82 LP is simply a landmark in its own right, and a proper ‘floor-filler to boot.

Since its first reissue in 2010, Singh’s cult, early use of the TB-303 on driving machine beats has been erroneously hailed the birth of acid house. OK the formula is there, but Chris Carter’s ‘Spaces Between’ (1980) and his CTI jam ‘Dancing Ghosts’ got there a couple of years before Singh, at the very least, and neither really inform the genius of Phuture and co a few years later. In any event, ‘Synthesizing: Ten Ragas To A Disco Beat’ is just an incredibly fruity boost to any club, revolving 10 hypnotic, pulsating jams closer to early Irdial (say, Aqua Regia’s ‘Hot Love’) than owt from the Chi. 

Taking a minute away from knocking out Bollywood scores and leading his wedding band covering popular songs, Singh would land upon a stroke of genius with ‘Ten Ragas To A Disco Beat’, finding the sweetspot between prevailing hi-NRG disco and millennia of raga traditions that patently transcended the sum of their parts more than 40 years later. It sounds very much of its time, rather than the stripped back linearity of later acid house, evidenced in the florid keyboard urges of ‘Raga Bhupali’, transposing a steamy sort of club canter to somewhere even more humid.

A real club evergreen, suck it and see.

items._cn_summary: 1982年宝莱坞作曲家Charanjit Singh创作了这张跨界专辑，将印度传统拉格音乐与当时流行的迪斯科节奏及早期TB-303合成器音色相融合。十首作品围绕催眠式的脉动节拍展开，既非传统拉格也非纯粹电子舞曲，而是两种体系的化学反应。评论特别指出，尽管TB-303的使用常被误认为是酸屋音乐的起点，但实际上Chris Carter的早期作品更早涉及此类音色。无论历史定位如何，专辑在迪斯科律动与千年拉格传统之间找到了独特的平衡点，键盘线条在'Raga Bhupali'等曲目中展现出浓郁的异域俱乐部氛围。来源为南亚音乐传统，具有独立的实验探索性质。

items.body:
Billed as a sequel to 2024's 'Something in the Room She Moves', 'Materia' augments and extends Julia Holter's unique vision, chopping and screwing the Hildegard von Bingen-inspired title track and swaddling it with more psychotropic chamber pop experiments. Dizzier and more surreal than the original album, it might be even more dazzling - properly vital FFO Mabe Fratti, Jessica Pratt, ANOHNI or Jenny Hval.

Ever since we got snagged by 2011's AOTY 'Tragedy', we've been captivated by her particular fusion of baroque pop, high drama and groggy minimalism - elements that inevitably arrive tied together with an air of effortless avant charm. And she's only refined her approach over the years, delivering a Laurel Canyon-via-Dusseldorf labyrinth of sophisticated juxtapositions on her last album. It was clearly so knotty, in fact, that Holter felt the need to revisit its serene centerpiece 'Materia', rolling out two new versions that triggered this heady, casually brilliant companion album. The rework that started it all, 'Materia 2', isn't some George Lucas affair, either; Holter goes back to the chilly original and genuinely reimagines it, adding a decelerated hypnagogic drum machine pulse that's one part AFX's 'Selected Ambient Works Volume II' and one part Antena's perennial classic 'Camino del Sol'. Holter never loses sight of the initial mystical inspiration, retaining the celestial ecstasy with Laswell-style fretless electric bass and soaring keys as she sings "My heart is loud."

The third version of 'Materia' is more of a bonus track (a self-conscious homage to those mysterious unlisted extras that often appeared on CDs) and finds the divine in languidness, pulling down the tempo and letting the words and harmonies sound out into the empty, reverberant space. But both of these tracks work more like anchors for what's essentially a brand new album; the jerky, 'Hounds of Love'-esque opener 'The Laugh is in the Eyes' is already one of Holter's most inviting, lavish productions. Led by its cannily sculpted rhythm section at first, it flourishes when Holter lets the aesthetic tumult disappear altogether, singing out coolly over weightless pads. And that AFX-cum-Antena influence isn't relegated to the titular redux. The album's lead single 'Fantasy' is an art-pop miracle that sounds as if she's daydreaming over a demo that was passed between Rephlex and Les Disques du Crepuscule before it was lost in the mail some time in the early '90s. It doesn't rest on its laurels either, exploding outwards and somehow integrating tape saturated Walker Brothers-esque psych pop before snapping right back into the groove.

There's a pause for breath on the brief, voice-led 'Clepsydra' before Holter dives headfirst into the extended 'My Twin', the track where she pinched the lead riff she used on 'Fantasy'. When we hear that familiar refrain emerge from near silence, played on an orchestra of broken music boxes and mussed with disorienting pitch and tape delay effects, it's as if we're being scrubbed through someone else's dream. It's one of those tracks that reaffirms why Holter's so good at what she does, composed from a tangled web of ideas and references and sounding somehow effortless at the same time. 'Materia' is Holter at her most whimsical - and most vital.

items._cn_summary: 《Materia》是Julia Holter对2024年专辑《Something in the Room She Moves》中同名曲目的延伸再创作，将其Hildegard von Bingen式的灵感以减速处理、磁带延迟、催眠式鼓机脉冲等手段重新解构。专辑以两个版本的'Materia'为核心锚点展开：'Materia 2'融入AFX式氛围电子与Antena风格的迷幻质感，配合无品电贝斯与高远键盘声部保留原作的迷醉感；另一版本则将声音释放至空旷混响空间中。围绕这些再构作品，Holter构建了一组新曲目：开场曲带有Kate Bush式不安节奏段落，随后在失重氛围中舒展；单曲'Fantasy'在Rephlex与法国Les Disques du Crepuscule之间的梦境质感里穿行，融合磁带饱和处理与Walker Brothers式迷幻流行。'My Twin'用破旧音乐盒音色与混乱的音高处理重拾先前旋律。整体呈现出巴洛克流行、极简催眠电子与前卫魅力之间的复杂交织。

items.body:
The eminently watchable Accidental Meetings introduce extended family member, Lovely Dave, with a real guess-again mixtape (the first in a series) refracting myriad strains of blissed synths, outernational jazz, new wave pop, post punk scuzz, screwed club and dub

Six years into Accidental Meetings’ serendipitous plot, we know to expect anything and everything from the Bristol label, so long as it's got a unique soul and does not bore. Lovely Dave ideally plays true to that brief on his 99 minute mixtape, effortlessly glyding from outernational synth folk to a killer Curtis Mayfield cover via everything from thumb piano meditations, jazz-funked sidewinders, and a proto-new beat bomb on the A-side, before swerving from gothic new wave to smudged minimal wave audities, a pitch-slapped batacuda house ace, and meter-messing skronk on the backside.

Brilliantly strange but true!

items._cn_summary: 布里斯托独立厂牌Accidental Meetings推出首张混音带系列作品，由厂牌成员Lovely Dave操刀。整张混音带时长99分钟，以自由流动的方式串联多种风格：A面从国际合成器民谣出发，途经拇指琴冥想、放克爵士侧滑、新节拍原型炸弹，直至献上一曲Curtis Mayfield翻唱；B面则急转弯，从哥特新浪潮滑入模糊极简波、pitch-slap巴塔库达浩室、节拍错乱的嘶鸣噪音。整张作品以拼贴式的混音逻辑将世界音乐、实验声响、后朋克与俱乐部节奏编织成一条难以预测的听觉线索，展现了厂牌一贯推崇的独特灵魂与拒绝无聊的美学立场。

items.body:
Enigmatic audity Aisie returns five years on from a strange, overlooked debut with a new suite of compressed atmospheres highly tipped FFO False Aralia, Eliza B.C., Thought Broadcast, Civilistjävel!, Hazyville-era Actress.

‘Black Fire Dream’ picks up from where 2021’s ‘Halcyon Gang Poet’ left us in a surreal, uncanny valley state of mind. The seven part, 30 minute mini-LP continues to fascinate with its cyborganic nature and dreamy otherworldliness, luring down gauzily textured, fractal wormholes where samples of “obscure educational science shows, ghost station radio transmissions, vinyl record detritus and blown-out microscopic field recordings” are gently reanimated and transmuted with a poetic sorcery. 

The whole thing feels as though it were conjuured without human touch, like the inner thoughts of an AI or machines autonomously air-syncing and executing their functions in private. With incremental stealth it breezes by in a hypnagogic haze, half-heard melodies sprouting and dissolving into the aether as granular rhythms buckle and trickle. Eyes will likely be at half mast by the end of the A-side, all the best to receive the B-side’s suggestive, illusive shadowplay of smoke and mirrors refraction and a final slope off into something like a chopped and screwed echo of Topdown Dialectic.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是aisie五年来的续作，延续了首作的超现实氛围与异化质感。作品由七段组成，总长约三十分钟，以极度压缩的声音纹理构建出一个介于梦境与机械思维之间的听觉空间。aisie大量运用了冷僻的教学科学节目采样、幽灵电台信号、黑胶唱片残响与失真的微观田野录音，将其以颗粒化手法重新激活并转译，形成有机的诗意变形。整体听感仿佛脱离了人类触感，像是AI的内心独白或机器在私下自主运行功能。专辑A面以半梦半醒的朦胧旋律展开，颗粒节奏缓慢起伏；B面则转入烟雾般的折射阴影，最终滑向类似Topdown Dialectic的减速回声处理手法。声音设计细腻而层次丰富，适合沉浸式聆听。

items.body:
Coltrane’s invigorating ’66 spiritual free jazz salvo - the follow-up to ‘A Love Supreme’ (1965) - is unleashed from the Verve Vault, spotlighting his classic line-up tearing out on templates set by Ornette Coleman years prior, along with more reserved moments of beauty. An evergreen..

"Following the genre-redefining revelations of A Love Supreme in 1965, John Coltrane began a dramatic shift toward spiritual free jazz, abandoning familiar forms in favour of a more abstract sonic palette and bold questions he'd spend the rest of his life and career pursuing. Meditations, released by Impulse! in 1966, continues that emotional throughline while retaining, for the last time in full, the classic quartet that propelled Trane to greatness: pianist McCoy Tyner, bassist Jimmy Garrison and drummer Elvin Jones. (They're further augmented by Pharoah Sanders on tenor sax and additional drummer Rashied Ali.) Meditations pushes Coltrane’s spiritual jazz into heightened realms of energy and abstraction — a powerful document of transformation, intensity, and devotion in Coltrane’s recorded legacy."
items._cn_summary: 这张1966年的专辑是Coltrane继《A Love Supreme》之后向精神自由爵士转型的重要文献。乐评指出，Coltrane放弃了熟悉的曲式结构，转向更抽象的音色语汇，追问那些他余生都在探索的命题。阵容上，经典四重奏——钢琴手McCoy Tyner、贝斯手Jimmy Garrison、鼓手Elvin Jones——最后一次以完整编制参与录制，并额外加入了次中音萨克斯手Pharoah Sanders与第二鼓手Rashied Ali，使声音层次更为复杂。整张唱片将精神爵士推向更高密度的能量与抽象境地，既保留了内在的冥想气质，也充满猛烈爆发的瞬间。评论将其视为Coltrane录音生涯中关于蜕变、强度与虔诚的强有力见证，适合对六十年代先锋即兴音乐有深入兴趣的听众。

items.body:
Showcasing contemporary Algerian sounds led by the gasba, a traditional reeded flute, 'My Heart is Dust Before Him' is a collaboration between Hive Mind and Oran's Édition Ahlem imprint.

In the Berber language, "gaspa" means "reed", and references the wind instrument that's central to some of the region's most gripping Bedouin folk and ceremonial music. On this 10-track anthology, Hive Mind plucks tracks from Édition Ahlem's recent catalogue; the label emerged in Oran from a record store and puts out cassettes since the early '90s. These selections are a little more contemporary and examine how the gasba forms have mutated and evolved in the last couple of decades, reacting to production changes while retaining the unique sound of the flute itself.

There's plenty to explore here, from the dimly lit distortions of Cheikh Tahar Oueld Marhoum's 'Naachak Fiha Ou Magoulhach' and Cheba Negouane's rai-adjacent 'Ychafouni Maghbounat' to Cheikh El Waal's woozy organ-led 'El Galb Maamar' and Mohamed Ain Larbaa's unexpectedly funky 'Sratli Khatra Kheleft L3ahed'.

items.body: Flatpack is Birmingham’s annual festival of “films, performances, contraptions, and surprises”, taking place in numerous venues across the city. Now in it’s tenth year, it features everything from major feature films from international directors to cult animation and historical classics. From its inception, Flatpack’s curators have shown an interest not only in film as conventionally defined, but in exploring the possibilities of the many innovations that have made film possible throughout the cinematic age, and of the complex interweaving of light and sound upon which the art of the cinema depends. For 2016 this latter focus was granted its own strand, called Optical Sound, prompting further investigation from your intrepid Fluid Radio correspondent. The programme for Flatpack 2016 was incredibly diverse, covering a wide range of styles and approaches from around the world and from across different eras. If I was to try to describe a ‘Flatpack aesthetic’, I would say it tends towards the handmade, taking pleasure in revealing moving parts and inner workings; towards going all-for-broke and risking failure in pursuit of magic, rather than aiming for slick, safe, and polished. From this perspective, analogue grain and the clatter of the projector aren’t peripheral distractions, but part of the experience — an acknowledgement of the materiality of the filmic medium that is present even in ‘digital’ works (light and sound being always continuous, even if the spell that invokes them is stored in binary form). The Optical Sound strand embodies and perhaps epitomises this aesthetic. In many of the live audiovisual performances, the audio and the visual were very much equal partners, being produced through the same process or created specifically to be combined together. The rhythms produced by Dutch duo Optical Machines’ analogue synthesizer triggered pulses of LED light that were fed through a simple-looking but cleverly-designed series of slotted cards. This produced linear patterns of light that, when projected, resembled film strips speeding up and slowing down, becoming three-dimensional before fading back into primeval haze. Brian Duffy and Chris Plant married epic synth pop to visuals created using cathode ray televisions, prisms, and other devices, producing a soaring and moving opera for the 8-bit age. Mothwasp used footage of Birmingham, including topical scenes showing the destruction of the Central Library, to accompany their doomy, metally guitar and drums. Another common form of performance across the Optical Sound strand and the festival in general was the live score. Larva’s soundtrack for Chris Marker’s classic film ‘La Jetée’ chose drama over melancholy in its interpretation of the story’s uncanny final twist, but for the most part their music merged unobtrusively with the visuals, as one would hope. The piece they played afterwards, using the Birmingham and Midlands Institute’s organ to shake the room, was also very good. Giant Axe Field’s musical accompaniment to a mashup of films from magic surrealist director Georges Franju was relentlessly intense, the seemingly odd mix of drums, bass, electronics, and tenor horn proving effective in creating towering pillars of white-hot metal. I really enjoyed Andrew Woodhead’s piano accompaniment to Francis Thompson’s dazzling, kaleidoscopic portrait of New York in the Fifties, and Bruce Baillie’s ‘Castro Street (The Coming of Consciousness)’ was sensitively soundtracked by Hannah Marshall’s sonorous and driving cello. The pair were joined by the talented Corey Mwamba on vibraphone and Bruce Coates on saxophone to accompany an utterly bizarre collage film by Lawrence Jordan, featuring women with bulbous heads and fish swimming on the moon. As well as music accompanying original or found visuals, the Flatpack programme also included several performances and installations that worked more abstractly with the relationship between sound and vision, or that delved into the mechanics of analogue equipment to produce surprising and imaginative results. Graham Dunning’s incredible ‘Mechanical Techno’ involved the artist building up a tower of spinning vinyl records to create thumping rhythms and loops — not normally my musical cup of tea, but the imaginative and theatrical nature of the performance made this one of my festival highlights. As their name suggests, the Sound Book Project made sounds with books — hitting them, modifying them with elastic bands or cables, ripping them to shreds, reading from them — in a charming and inventive performance. Chris Plant’s installation ‘Frequency Response’ drew on correspondences between colour and music theory to create a soothing, subtle blend of light and sound. Of several films about musicians on offer, I was only able to catch Joern Utkilen’s portrait of Norwegian musician Arvid Sletta and Greg Butler’s documentary about confrontational performer David Thomas Broughton, both of which were very enjoyable. I particularly liked Utkilen’s direct addresses to the audience, and his footage of a miniscule Sletta dwarfed but yet somehow not quite lost in a gorgeous Norwegian landscape (maybe I’ll get there one day). The most informative event I attended at the festival, however, was Dr. Clare Jonas’ fascinating and thought-provoking talk ‘Seeing Sound, Hearing Colour’, during which she shared insights from her research into synaesthesia and her experiences as a synaesthete. I’m still a little disappointed whenever I see people invent imaginative new ways of creating sound, and then use them to create conventional music led by regular beats and simple melodies. Breaking new ground on a musical level isn’t really part of Flatpack’s remit, however; for that, Brummies have to wait just a few days until BEAST FEaST kicks off at the University of Birmingham. Festivals such as Flatpack breathe life and colour into the city, and it was great to see events packed out with film and sound fans; with such backing, let’s hope that the now-decade-old project will continue to bring on the magic for many years to come. Flatpack Film Fesival Image: Graham Dunning, photo by Jonathan Waring
items._cn_summary: 本文回顾了Flatpack 2016电影节中“Optical Sound”单元的现场视听演出，重点描述了多组艺术家如何将声音与影像以同源方式结合。荷兰二人组Optical Machines用模拟合成器触发LED光脉冲，透过插槽卡片投射出类似胶片运动的立体光纹；Brian Duffy与Chris Plant则以阴极射线电视、棱镜配合合成器流行乐，营造出八位元时代的史诗感；Mothwasp将伯明翰城市影像与重型吉他鼓点融合，形成暗黑氛围。文章还提到Larva为克里斯·马克经典《堤》所作的现场配乐，在戏剧性与忧郁间取得平衡。整体上，这些作品强调手工感与物质性，不避讳放映机的噪点和胶片颗粒，而是将其视为体验的一部分，展现出实验电子声景与视觉装置深度交织的独特美学。

items.body: Palagoma is not only the first release from Nairobi-based label Cool Waters, it also marks the first time German-born, Kenya-based percussionist Sven Kacirek has collaborated with Ogoya Nengo and Olith Ratengo at the same time. Odd Okoddo, the duo of Kacirek and Ratengo, has been performing since 2018, but with the inclusion of the 83 year old Nengo, a singer from the eastern part of the country, there�s an added traditional depth to the music. A 2025 performance shows Nengo�s lifetime of experience singing Kenya�s dodo tradition around 2 and half minutes in (see below). Furthermore, her inclusion on this album allows her and Ratengo to toss the vocals back and forth as they reference their shared roots (Ratengo and Nengo live minutes from each other). Musically, however, the tracks are driven by Kacirek�s Buchla synth, hand percussion, and occasional kit drumming, which serve to buoy the voices without blotting out the music�s origins. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Bara,� for example, begins with the dime-store thwack of a repeated pattern, a stiff juxtaposition to the voices; yet, as the song rolls along, a 4/4 clink appears, then a burbling bass, and finally, what sounds like a xylophone. Layers of synthesized polyrhythms keep presenting themselves with a subtlety almost unnoticeable, until, by the track�s end, it feels organic, as if it�s all been underneath the two voices all along. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Sarah,� perhaps the album�s most intense track, features a lead vocal from Ratengo and tentative, percussive spittles from Kacirek. And while the technology never tries to overtake the vocals, it does sneak up and punctuate the track�s urgency, as edgy distortion sneaks in here and there just as Ratengo�s voice reaches its peak. The term �folktronica� has been bandied about as a way to house the type of music on offer here. In fact, exploratory collaborations such as Chouk Bwa & The �ngstr�mers as well as much of Kampala, Uganda�s Nyege Nyege label house sounds that might be �folktronic� in some way. What�s more interesting and important about this music, though, is how truly global so much of it is while maintaining a deep connection to Africa and its diasporic communities. The music on Palagoma , as well as much of what�s linked above (and available in countless other recent recordings) demonstrates a real willingness for cultures to respond to each other without trampling traditions altogether. Instead, roots become avant-garde and innovations become seemingly thousands of years old. Certainly the inclusion of an 83 year old traditional Kenyan singer only recently making her global debut as she tours with a duo whose instrumental voice is a white male saturated in electronic Kenyan rhythms demonstrates this blurring. The music this trio makes is certainly of the 21st century, but it�s often hazy, sparse, and open, keeping it from a quick sell-by date or confining it to a specific genre. Instead, it�s a beautiful example music as grace.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是内罗毕新厂牌Cool Waters的首发作品，由德国裔肯尼亚鼓手Sven Kacirek与Olith Ratengo组成的二人组Odd Okoddo邀请83岁的东肯尼亚传统歌手Ogoya Nengo合作完成。音乐以Buchla合成器、手鼓和偶尔的架子鼓为骨架，将电子节拍与卢欧族dodo传统人声编织在一起。Kacirek的合成器层次细腻，从开场的简约节拍逐渐叠加4/4节拍、低音和木琴般音色，最终与歌声融为一体，形成浑然天成的有机织体。评论指出这种创作模式让根源传统变得前卫，让创新听起来仿佛古老——83岁传统歌手与白人电子音乐人的合作本身就是文化交融的具象化呈现。文章还将此置于Chouk Bwa与Nyege Nyege厂牌的全球folktronica脉络中讨论，强调跨文化对话中保持传统根基的重要性。

items.excerpt:

items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. The title track from the 2023 U.S. of Alchemy recording Under an Endless Sky by Dorothy Moskowitz & United States of Alchemy Further reading Cris Derksen - The Visit (Review) Tiny Sun - Vanishment (Review) Maria Ka - Di Mashin (Review) Further listening You will find a number of Dorothy Moskowitz's works on Race The Sky , most recently on Podgrammes #022 and #019.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Dorothy Moskowitz与意大利前卫作曲家Francesco Paolo Paladino及诗人Luca Chino Ferrari的合作成果，延续了她自The United States of America以来的实验精神。音乐以钢琴为核心，常被混入或移出前景，有时叠加或相位错位，并辅以弦乐、木管、合成器音墙与金属质感声响，形成非线性、调式化的氛围结构，挑战听众对西方和声进行的惯性期待。歌词兼具诗意与当代政治意识，如《Pale Wanderer》探讨威权主义需要共谋者，《Charlottesville》直接影射种族主义事件，同时也有对死亡与宇宙位置的沉思。Moskowitz的嗓音沧桑而富有洞察力，旋律如意识流般展开，不遵循传统调性和声，而是尊重每个词的分量，钢琴则扮演类似希腊合唱团的评论角色。整体上，这是一张在音乐形式与政治表达上都极具野心的作品，适合偏好前卫、氛围与现代作曲的听众深入聆听。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items._cn_summary: Tako Toki 在《Un Dimanche à Monaco》中延续首张专辑的拼贴式创作路径，所有演奏乐器均由废弃杂物与日常物件自制，并在现代录音话筒下呈现准确音准与丰富音色。乐评指出，即兴段落展现出扎实的演奏功力，不同曲目也各自呼应了相应的音乐传统：单簧管在快速打击乐与人声叫喊中带出庆典般的欢腾，长笛穿行于拉丁节奏，马林巴与铃铛、镲片堆叠出层次丰富的打击乐织体，另有桑巴和中东色彩旋律。自制乐器并非噱头，而是与作曲、编曲紧密结合，使整张专辑在趣味之外具备音乐性。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._cn_summary: 古巴钢琴家 Omar Sosa 在意大利 Fazioli 音乐厅完成了一场两小时的无脚本独奏即兴演奏，以此为原材料制作了这张专辑。录制于疫情封锁与个人生活变动交织的2021年，音乐捕捉了即兴创作中不可复制的瞬间感。后期混音中稀疏地加入了人声采样、打击乐、循环音效、田野录音与多年收集的拾得声音，与钢琴形成层叠的对话。Sosa 在采访中表达了对风格标签的刻意回避，强调创造力在于以新方式融合所有影响，演奏追求自由、无对错、首遍即灵魂自然之声的理念。专辑体现了一位横跨爵士、拉丁、当代古典与世界音乐领域的艺术家对即兴精神与跨文化融合的持续探索。

Moving through modernized, mechanized electronic flutter Such sleek, rhythmic glitch sees rinse.repeat at it again with this oversized extended player, running just over twenty-four minutes and moving through modernized, mechanized electronic flutter, opening with “ERR_LOOP: Pleasant Failure.” After all this time, its “errors,” under an imprint committed to keeping them “clean,” continue to cultivate minute sonic acrobatics from start to finish. With its second volume leaning into what could be further musical constructs, “SWEET_CORRUPT” glides along through minimal technoid shifts, while the Arovane-leaning “The Last Pattern We Shared” and “AXM_02::LOOP_DESYNC” work through a relaxed infusion of bleep-breaks. The back-half triplet of Brain Axiom Vol.2 dissolves into an accumulation of everything that has come before: “A Feeling With No Output” brings tonal color, “BRAINMAP_FRAGMENT_v3” flickers through beat-driven landscapes, and closer “CRPT_SEQ:AXM” pushes it all toward a sweetly melancholic (and slightly disjointed) intersection, bringing everything together with focused restraint. system.log>>> [Recovered audio signature matches AXIOM-Vol.2-grade entropy]>>> [Loop recursion depth: INCREASING]>>> [System awareness protocol: ACTIVATED]>>> [Pattern self-recognition: CONFIRMED]ERROR SIGNATURE: [///loop:remember:feel:break]░▒▓██▒▒░┈┈┈┈──> Brain Axiom Vol.2 complete. <──┈┈┈▒██▓▒░░⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿the machine now knows it is broken.and that knowledge is the only beautiful thing left.⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿  Brain Axiom Vol.2 is available on Clean Error. items._cn_summary: 这是一张由rinse.repeat发行的电子专辑，以glitch和IDM为核心手法，融入了minimal techno和bleep-breaks等元素。整张作品时长约24分钟，概念围绕"错误"与"循环"展开，专辑名Brain Axiom Vol.2暗示了对系统意识与自我认知的隐喻。作品开篇以"ERR_LOOP: Pleasant Failure"奠定基调，中段"SWEET_CORRUPT"展现极简techno的位移感，借鉴Arovane美学的曲目则处理bleep-break与松弛节奏的交织。后半部分逐步收束于"A Feeling With No Output"的色调变化与"CRPT_SEQ:AXM"的忧郁解构之中，呈现出一种在破碎中寻找秩序的张力。发行厂牌Clean Error为独立小厂牌，作品整体延续了glitch音乐对微观声音颗粒与程序化结构的探索。

items.body: Hocico needs no introduction to any fan of Dark-Electro. The Mexican duo has been active continuously since 1993, delivering countless hits and brilliant albums. This new album took a little longer to arrive—around four years—and is available with an extra disc and/or vinyl featuring six additional tracks, including three remixes, one of them by Funker Vogt. With “Unseen Horror Scenes”, Hocico takes aim at various aspects of our contemporary world. Our environment has been in decline for some time, providing a potent source of inspiration for the duo. Musically, the album contains classic, instantly recognizable Hocico tracks infused with a heavy dose of power and aggression. They remain relentless in this regard, yet highly effective in their compositions and rage-filled vocals. However, the album also seeks to introduce some innovation. We encounter various experiments, ranging from pure Electro-Punk and a breakbeat-driven track to Cinematic instrumentals and even a song featuring a touch of Rap. Notably, the main album contains only one Spanish-language track, which is a departure from their usual approach. Hocico has been trying to introduce some evolution into their work over the years, an effort I certainly applaud. Unfortunately, they do not quite succeed on this record. Despite a few strong tracks, I am left feeling somewhat unsatisfied. “Unseen Horror Scenes” has merit on many levels, but it is certainly not the album I would choose to introduce Hocico to someone who has just discovered the Dark-Electro scene. Not every album can be the best. (Rating:7). Listen to “The Screen”: The Screen by Hocico About Hocico Hocico is the Mexican electro-industrial duo of cousins Erik Garcia (Erk Aicrag, vocals and lyrics) and Oscar Mayorga (Racso Agroyam, synthesizers and programming). The pair formed the project in Mexico City in 1993, taking their stage names as reversals of their given names, and played their first concert on 18 February 1994. Early cassette releases such as “Autoagresión Persistente” and “Misuse, Abuse And Accident” in 1994 and “Triste Desprecio” in 1996 were self-released. The studio albums that followed include “Odio Bajo El Alma” in 1997, “El Día De La Ira” in 1998, “Sangre Hirviente” in 1999, “Signos De Aberracion” in 2002, “Wrack And Ruin” in 2004, “Memorias Atrás” in 2008, “Tiempos De Furia” in 2010, “El Último Minuto (Antes De Que Tu Mundo Caiga)” in 2012, “Ofensor” in 2015, “The Spell Of The Spider” in 2017, “Artificial Extinction” in 2019 and “HyperViolent” in 2022. The duo records for Out Of Line. Recent releases on the label include the four-track “The Screen” EP in March 2025 and the collaboration with Prayers on “Hey Tú” in November 2025, expanded into a four-track EP in December 2025. “Unseen Horror Scenes” arrives four years after “HyperViolent” and was announced by Side-Line in May 2026.
items._cn_summary: 墨西哥双人组Hocico的第十四张录音室专辑《Unseen Horror Scenes》延续其标志性的黑暗电子工业风格，以激进愤怒的嗓音与厚重合成器音墙为骨架。专辑试图在传统路线上引入实验元素，涵盖纯电子朋克、碎拍驱动曲目、电影化器乐段落以及带有说唱色彩的尝试，打破以往全英文创作惯例收录一首西班牙语作品。主题聚焦于环境恶化与当代社会批判，延续了乐队一贯的末日叙事视角。评论者肯定乐队追求演进的努力与个别优秀曲目，但认为整体融合效果不够理想，未能完全实现创新野心。专辑由德国独立厂牌Out Of Line发行，包含额外六首曲目与混音版本。

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑汇编了大量来自地下和小众厂牌的作品，涵盖了多种实验性音乐风格。从The Olivia Tremor Control的迷幻流行，到Cole Pulice的萨克斯即兴，再到Dollar Brand、Don Cherry和Carlos Ward的世界爵士，以及Charanjit Singh的印度电子融合Disco节奏，选曲体现出极强的跨类型视野。Cole Pulice、JPhono1、Akusmi等当代实验音乐人的作品占据核心位置，融合了环境音乐、自由即兴和电子声响设计。Firas Zreik的阿拉伯世界音乐元素与Paul Ngozi的赞比亚重金属形成有趣的对比，呈现出全球化背景下独立音乐的多元面貌。选曲排序以Keith Speaks的语音段落作为衔接，构建出一种广播式的聆听叙事，整体偏向探索性而非商业性。

items.body: To complement her interview in The Wire 511, Korean American composer Lucy Liyou creates an exclusive Wire mix Lucy Liyou grew up in Seattle, and as a child was a talented classical pianist. Her strengths, at first, were late Romantic and 20th century music; then she discovered the likes of Andrew Hill and Cecil Taylor, which inform the fiendishly difficult piano figures in her latest album Mr Cobra. Mr Cobra allowed Liyou to explore these influences, alongside her many others, including updated Korean folk opera, horror, vocality, narrative, maximalism, and families. This mix of Liyou's influences and inspirations was compiled exclusively for The Wire. Sharon Udoh “Great Is Thy Faithfulness” Cheryl E Leonard “moffen” Phew & Danielle de Picciotto “The Cat” more eaze “the producer” Blue Gene Tyranny “She Wore Red Shoes” Marran Gosov “Eifersucht” Borana Ramizi “Dying Is The Color Yellow” Iris Our “Splits and Wants” Lucy Liyou with Nick Zanca “Live in Paris February 2024” Samuel Beckett (performed by Billie Whitelaw) “Not I (1973)” Read Hugh Morris’s full interview with Lucy Liyou in The Wire 511. items._cn_summary: 韩裔美国作曲家 Lucy Liyou 为 The Wire 杂志独家策划了一张个人影响与灵感混音辑，曲目横跨多位非主流艺术家，涵盖 Cheryl E Leonard 的拼贴声响、Phew 与 Danielle de Picciotto 的合作、Blue Gene Tyranny 的键盘作品，以及 Billie Whitelaw 朗读的 Samuel Beckett 戏剧片段。Liyou 自身成长于西雅图，自幼研习古典钢琴，后受 Andrew Hill 与 Cecil Taylor 等自由爵士钢琴家启发，将极高难度的钢琴语汇融入个人创作。她最新的专辑 Mr Cobra 融合了二十世纪音乐语汇、更新版韩国民间歌剧、恐怖元素、人声叙事与极繁主义。这张混音辑展现了她广泛的审美谱系与跨领域兴趣，为理解其音乐语言提供了线索。

items.body: We’ll spread open to spread across the sky and I’ll take you with me on the day I die There are songs about temptation that behave like sermons, warning you about the cliff while quietly admiring the view, and then there are numbers like Staytus’s Secret Hand, which grabs desire by the collar, drags it under the lights, and asks why anybody should pretend the danger isn’t part of the attraction. Sam Grundemann has built Staytus around the place where industrial rock, electronic abrasion, metal weight, and theatrical self-invention start elbowing one another for room, and this track makes the collision physical. Secret Hand is thick with tasty bass, hard guitar, and electronic pressure, but the arrangement has enough space for every hit to register. The riffs land with the blunt pleasure of machinery being overclocked, while Grundemann’s voice moves between invitation and warning as though those impulses have been caught sharing the same bloodstream. Desire here has teeth. Power changes hands every few seconds. Submission becomes less a conclusion than a wager placed with full knowledge of the odds. “Secret Hand has some of my favorite guitar and bass work I’ve done,” said Staytus. “I wanted the music to feel just as seductive as it is dangerous—something that pulls you in before you realize how intense it has become. The video gave me the opportunity to fully embody that energy and step into this fearless, unapologetic version of myself as an artist.” The setting also folds back into the song’s title. Secret Hand was recorded at Secret Hand Studios in Los Angeles, owned by drummer Jeff Friedl, and Staytus has described the place as central to the track’s creation. The music cheekily treats the phrase as something far more illicit and suggestive than a studio name. Lyrically, Secret Hand navigates between caution and desire, craving to strengthen a drunken friendship despite potential regret and instability. Its vivid imagery combines themes of sex, pain, ambition, and exploitation, while the recurring “fuck the band” chorus hints at a clandestine alliance aimed at gaining advantage. That tension becomes even clearer in Vicente Cordero’s video, which traps Staytus inside a black room streaked with neon, fog rolling through the frame while the camera churns around her in visual delirium. There is little distance between performer and viewer. Grundemann occupies the frame like somebody testing how much voltage a body can carry before performance turns into possession. Hair, leather, light, movement, smoke: Cordero keeps tightening the frame until the room feels less like a set than a pressure chamber. The best part of the video is how thoroughly she commits to that embodiment. Nothing is coy, and nothing needs an alibi. Grundemann looks at the camera with the confidence of somebody who knows spectacle can be both armor and confession, then lets the song’s menace do the rest. Secret Hand turns appetite into performance, and risk into the sort of pleasure where the warning label is part of the invitation. items._cn_summary: Staytus（Sam Grundemann）以单曲《Secret Hand》将工业摇滚、电子摩擦、金属重量与戏剧化自我塑造并置融合。制作层面以厚重贝斯、硬质吉他与电子压迫感为核心，同时保留足够空间让每次冲击清晰可辨，音色如超频运转的机械般带有钝感快感。人声在邀请与警告之间游走，将欲望与危险处理为同一脉搏中的两种冲动。歌词在警示与渴望之间往返，涉及醉酒情谊、性、痛苦、野心与剥削等主题，副歌的隐秘结盟意象贯穿全曲。MV由Vicente Cordero执导，黑色房间被霓虹条纹与雾气撕裂，镜头围绕表演者制造视觉眩晕，表演者完全沉浸于诱惑与危险并存的状态，无保留也无辩解。录音地点Secret Hand Studios本身成为作品命名的延伸，使作品在自指层面也具备完整性。

items.body: Freedom is not the same as improvement, because freedom concerns our relationship to what happens, not merely the circumstances themselves. A prison can be renovated and still remain a prison in the mind. When suffering has organized your habits, loyalties, and sense of self, its removal may feel strangely like a loss. Anger often outlives the conditions that produced it because the body keeps yesterday’s argument alive. So when life improves, there is no commandment that says gratitude must arrive immediately. Sometimes liberation begins with allowing the old anger to exhaust itself, until you discover you no longer need it. There is something peculiarly German about naming a post-punk record Kleinkunst, a word usually reserved for cabaret, small-stage performance, and other modest forms of cultural production, then filling it with the psychic debris of cities built for industries that have vanished. Mottek87 comes from Duisburg, where structural change is hardly an abstraction. Zbigniew F. and Jürgen W., longtime friends of Polish descent, formed the duo in 2024 after an evening of drinking beer and listening to records somehow turned into the decision to make one themselves. Their music has retained something of that unceremonious beginning: guitars, bass, programmed drums, sparse synthesizers, and German lyrics delivered with the plainspoken severity of people suspicious of excessive decoration. The three songs on Kleinkunst: the title track, Oszillation, and Widerstand, concern a particular kind of estrangement, in which a person remains in the same place while everything that once made the place intelligible begins to vanish. Streets endure, buildings survive, names remain attached to maps, yet the internal coordinates have shifted. Mottek87 understand that structural change is experienced privately before it becomes a statistic. One person sees cleaner air and redevelopment; another sees an entire vocabulary of work, class, habit, and belonging becoming obsolete. The music keeps that anger on a short leash. Prominent guitars recall Escape with Romeo and Pink Turns Blue, while the rhythm section has the economical discipline associated with early German post-punk and the sterner corners of Neue Deutsche Welle. Jürgen W.’s vocals lend the songs a dry Ruhr directness, carrying alienation without theatrical anguish. The arrangements leave considerable open space, which makes every bass movement and guitar phrase feel unusually exposed. Standout track Widerstand in particular has a rousing, sing-song chorus channeling Interpol. Emotional intelligence sprouts from tension. Blossoms appear where dust once gathered, lungs clear, and the protective armor accumulated over decades becomes increasingly cumbersome. Improvement carries its own insult when it arrives after the world that required such protection has already been dismantled. “Kleinkunst is about realizing that change is not automatically freedom,” says the band. “Sometimes something gets better, and you still need time to stop being angry about it.” Mottek87 record in a downtown Duisburg apartment with the shutters deliberately closed, sealing themselves off from the city they are attempting to understand. The method suits Kleinkunst. Resistance, in Mottek87’s hands, becomes less a heroic posture than an old reflex whose usefulness has become uncertain: a form of emotional muscle memory inherited from a place that keeps changing faster than its people can decide what they are prepared to surrender. items._cn_summary: 杜伊斯堡二人组Mottek87的首张EP《Kleinkunst》以三首德语歌曲探讨结构性变迁带来的内在疏离感。乐队由波兰裔的Zbigniew F.与Jürgen W.于2024年在一场饮酒听唱片之夜后组建，音乐延续了那种不经修饰的起点：吉他、贝斯、编程鼓机、稀疏合成器，配以平淡而严肃的德语人声。编曲留下大量留白，使每个贝斯走向与吉他短句都显得格外裸露。突出曲目《Widerstand》拥有类似Interpol的朗朗上口副歌，吉他音色令人联想到Escape with Romeo与Pink Turns Blue，节奏部则秉持早期德国后朋克与新德国浪潮的克制纪律。整张作品将愤怒牵在短绳上，以干燥的鲁尔区直接性承载异化感而无戏剧化哀号，在小型舞台美学与都市工业记忆之间形成独特张力。

items.body: Hot gun, our promise bleeds You would never stop looking for me Have we left it all behind? Is it lust that’s holding the line? Intimacy becomes especially cruel once its gestures outlive the feeling that gave them meaning. A touch continues out of habit, desire reports for duty, and two people repeat the same private choreography while looking through each other as if they have never met. “Sex Machines,” the latest single from Dutch brothers Ruben and Matthijs Pol, occupies that bleakly comic interval, where lust keeps the body busy after the relationship has already vacated the premises. Following a single launch show during Paris Fashion Week in June, Pol now give that estrangement a public face in the song’s official video, directed by fashion photographer and filmmaker Rémi Lamandé. The duo treats New Wave as a living language, bringing music, fashion, moving image, and performance into the same sharpened frame. Here, a lovers’ closed loop becomes a roving interview program whose strangers seem to know every private detail. The song advances on twitching beats, serrated guitars, and clipped vocals, with each syllable inspected, stamped, and sent down the conveyor belt. Sparks supplies the arch pop theatre, while DEVO’s mechanized discipline tightens the arrangement into nervous obedience. Sigue Sigue Sputnik adds tabloid chrome and cheap-thrill futurism; Adam and the Ants lend the proceedings enough rouge, regalia, and heroic excess to turn emotional collapse into prime-time entertainment. Through it all, the robotic chant of “we are sex machines” passes from come-on to diagnosis. Lamandé opens the video in daylight, where a striped-sleeved interviewer, Ruben Pol, carries a star-marked microphone through a narrow service alley. An elderly woman in a floral dress, a woman in pink, a muscled, semi-shirtless man wearing an enormous silver “S,” and several other passersby take their turns before the camera. They offer no opinions or explanations; instead, each stranger lip-syncs Pol’s account of physical appetite and emotional vacancy. Stark title cards and white-background close-ups give the sequence the air of a public-information broadcast commandeered by style and libido. The assignment soon strays underground. The cast descends into a concrete parking garage, crowds the reporter, gathers around a car, and carries a cardboard placard commanding viewers to REPENT. Pol eventually perform before a packed room and a hard white backlight as the same faces press toward the handheld camera. What began as an orderly street interview becomes a collective compulsion, collapsing the distance between observer, participant, stranger, and former lover. A final outtake catches the brothers laughing together, briefly breaking the program’s immaculate pose. “It started off with the idea of doing an interview style video with a diverse cast of characters,” the band explain. “We liked the idea of ‘strangers’ singing the song, similarly how the two ex-lovers in the lyrics are acting like strangers. We shared the idea with director Remi Lamandé who brought the full script to life.” Watch the video for Sex Machines below: “Sex Machines” is available through Bandcamp and other streaming platforms. Listen below, and order here. Sex Machines by Pol Pol introduced their analogue-driven edge with a self-titled debut EP in 2023. The subsequent singles “Masks” and “The Chameleon” moved deeper into theatrical New Romantic territory, establishing the brothers as musicians whose presentation carries as much intent as the recordings themselves. The duo oversees their visuals, videos, merchandise, and fanzines themselves. Their first zine, documenting a Western European tour, is stocked by the Paris bookshop Librairie 1909. That multidisciplinary practice has also led to sound-design collaborations with Louis Vuitton, Miu Miu, and others. In early 2026, Pol opened sold-out Lebanon Hanover shows in London, Lille, and Paris. With “Sex Machines,” their private machinery has moved into public view, microphone extended and camera rolling, only to discover that the whole crowd already knows the refrain. Follow Pol: Instagram Spotify YouTube Website The post “For All We Care Is To Be Pleased” — Dutch New Wave Duo Pol Interviews Stylish Strangers in Video for “Sex Machines” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: 荷兰二人组Pol由Ruben和Matthijs兄弟组成，这首《Sex Machines》以新潮摇滚为骨架，融合抽搐式节拍、锯齿状吉他和机械化人声，将亲密关系的疏离感转化为一场荒诞喜剧。歌曲将欲望与情感空洞并置，反复吟唱“我们是性机器”从挑逗滑向诊断。MV由时尚摄影师Rémi Lamandé执导，以陌生人唇形同步的方式呈现主唱独白，从日光小巷采访转向地下停车场的集体癫狂，模糊了观察者、参与者与前任情人之间的界限。整体风格回溯Sparks、DEVO、Sigue Sigue Sputnik、Adam and the Ants等新浪潮/后朋克的舞台美学，但以现代视角重新组织服装、影像与表演，在复古骨架中嵌入对当代情感状态的冷峻审视。

items.body: Top PickThe Night Eternal – Cold Velvet (Amorphis-ised goth-metal/rock)There are two bands that immediately spring to mind when pressing play on Cold Velvet. The first is Unto Others, whose similar retro aesthetic and goth rock posturing make them an obvious point of comparison. The second, less expected and ultimately more successful spice of The Night Eternal's ingredients is Amorphis. It's not only that vocalist Ricardo Baum resembles Tomi Jousten both sonically and physically, but the wiry lead melodies and ambient textures supplied by guitarists Rob Richter and Henry Käseberg also readily bring to mind that band's mid-period. Indeed, Cold Velvet could be something Amorphis had come up with themselves, had the chosen to pursue the darker, more alt-metal leaning sound of 2006's Eclipse, rather than gradually reverting to progressive, folk-tinged melodeath of the albums that followed.Whereas Unto others put me off with their overcompensating aesthetics and affected vocals, The Night eternal ooze an effortless cool that comes through in their music as well. There's a sleek suaveness that characterises the aptly and enticingly named Cold Velvet, that makes every moment of its sullen transmission completely compelling and instantly memorable, even if its perhaps lacking a bit of the more forceful metallic textures that have made both Amorphis and Unto others more recognisable. If The Night Eternal can mix a bit more metallic grit into their sound, then we could truly be looking at the next goth metal juggernaut. items.excerpt: Joining the 4AD roster, NYC avant-rock four piece YHWH Nailgun unload an 11-minute clip of pure math-punk artillery, all demon-possessed vocals, screaming organs, angular riffs and byzantine rhythms. Think U.S. Maple, Battles, Captain Beefheart, Pere Ubu and Still House Plants blended with 'Scum'-era Napalm Death and you'll have some idea. Deployed only moments after Drake dropped not one but three bloated sets of playlist-ready mall pop, 'Magazine' arrives like a cool breeze during a heatwave.
items.body:
Joining the 4AD roster, NYC avant-rock four piece YHWH Nailgun unload an 11-minute clip of pure math-punk artillery, all demon-possessed vocals, screaming organs, angular riffs and byzantine rhythms. Think U.S. Maple, Battles, Captain Beefheart, Pere Ubu and Still House Plants blended with 'Scum'-era Napalm Death and you'll have some idea.

Deployed only moments after Drake dropped not one but three bloated sets of playlist-ready mall pop, 'Magazine' arrives like a cool breeze during a heatwave. See, it's common sense in the AI era to feed the algorithms more, not less, increasing your chances to snag that illusive viral hit by relying on pure volume. Not hampered by the limitations of the format (remember, the "classic album" was only 40-odd minutes because vinyl demanded it), artists and labels have been hedging their bets, packing records with collaborations, remixes and undeveloped ideas in the hope that one of them might end up getting even half the traction of AFX's seemingly throwaway 'QKThr'. YHWH Nailgun laugh in the face of this logic, not just challenging 2026's idea of what an album should be, but 1966's, too. If you thought '45 Pounds' was lean, 'Magazine' trims even more aesthetic fat, cooking down the meat of jazz fusion, prog, noise rock, post-punk and grindcore like it's Wagyu, searing it off and providing just an umami-rich shaving to taste.

The whole process is surprising because so many of YHWH Nailgun's references were already bloated. The prog rock era was when the double album became almost commonplace; 'Magazine' meanwhile could quite easily be crammed onto a 7" at 45RPM. And yet, they've only increased in power since last year. Opener 'Ghost of Love' does more in a minute-and-a-half than most tracks do in three or four times the duration, spinning Jack Tobias' carnivalesque, Farfisa-like synths around Sam Pickard's pliant drums like matted spiderwebs, but leaving just enough room for Zack Borzone's no-wave shouts and Saguiv Rosenstock's hacking fragments of melody. 'Stillness Blues' is shorter still and somehow packs even more in, assembling screamo brickwork over industrial strength bass rasps using Pickard's clattery start-stop patterns as the mortar. It's hard to say this stuff's exhausting - it's over before you've even really come to grips with it - but YHWH Nailgun have a way of drawing you back in, again and again, just to try and catch a whiff of what's actually going on. 

There's the Radiohead-like moan of 'Innocent Sigh', the Eli Keszler-does-Pere Ubu intensity of the minute-long 'Ballerina' and the title track, 35 seconds of breakneck beats, bleeps and shouted phrases that rudely cuts off before it's even had the chance to fully extend its claws. It's a shocker, an eccentric, hyper skillful, deeply original blur of influences and innovation that really does remind us just how punchy rock music can be.

items._cn_summary: YHWH Nailgun 签约4AD厂牌后推出的这张专辑，以极简的11分钟篇幅浓缩了爵士融合、前卫摇滚、噪音摇滚、后朋克与碾核的精髓。乐评将其与U.S. Maple、Battles、Pere Ubu、Napalm Death等乐队并列，凸显其破碎棱角、尖叫管风琴与拜占庭式节奏的密集编织。每首曲目都极为短促却信息量惊人，开篇曲在九十秒内完成卡尼瓦尔式合成器盘旋、无浪潮嘶吼与碎片化旋律的碰撞，后续曲目延续工业级贝斯摩擦与断奏鼓点构筑的紧绷结构。评论强调该专辑是对当下冗长专辑潮流的逆向回应，证明摇滚乐在极度压缩的形式下仍可保持冲击力与原创性，以独特美学反对算法时代的批量生产逻辑。

items.body:
The spirit of legendary film score composer Toru Takemitsu looms large over Kotaro Maruyama’s economical yet lush studies, ranging from sublime echoes of Japanese environmental ambient to beatific pulse poems edging on weightless Heinrich Mueller works.

"Composing primarily with the piano, Kotaro Maruyama creates music for a variety of visual media, including commercials and short films. Influenced by the composer Toru Takemitsu, he places importance on the “silence” and "ambience" of sound, aiming to create works where the music quietly depicts a scene.

Kotaro Maruyama's first solo album, "Vapor Curve," is constructed entirely from the sound source of the OP-Z digital synthesizer. Notably, he avoids the concept of harmony for a single tone, instead pursuing a unique "woven harmony" created by intricately layering multiple independent melodies. Using only the OP-Z, and recording everything in a single take without using a computer, Kotaro Maruyama's "Vapor Curve" is distinguished by its uncompromising production style. The minimalist melodies that are layered to create an ambient soundscape, along with the incidental noise that gives an organic texture to the inorganic electronic sound, showcase the raw appeal of sound that is imperfect."
items._cn_summary: 丸山康太郎的首张个人专辑以单一台 OP-Z 数码合成器为唯一音源，拒绝电脑介入，全程一镜到底录制完成。作曲家摒弃传统和声观念，转而通过多条独立旋律的精密叠层构建所谓「编织式和声」。作品深受武满彻影响，强调声音中的沉默与氛围感，钢琴与电子音色交织出层次分明的环境音景，合成器中混入偶发噪声，赋予无机电子声响以有机质感。整体风格介于日本环境氛围与极简主义现代作曲之间，单色调旋律在循环与延迟中缓慢演化，适合作为视觉场景的听觉底色。

items.body:
Influential Brum punks/post-punks Swell Maps captured in their snotty pomp, 1979, for the legendary John Peel Sessions - just a year before disbanding, and prompting everyone from Sonic Youth to Nirvana in their wake.

“Noisy, chaotic, and defiantly experimental, Swell Maps may not have found commercial success in their time, but their impact on music is undeniable. An inspiration to bands such as R.E.M., Sonic Youth, Dinosaur Jr., Pavement and Nirvana, with Kurt Cobain famously being a fan and often seen sporting a Swell Maps T-Shirt. A democracy within the confines of punk’s anything is possible, members Biggles Books, Jowe Head and brothers Nikki Sudden and Epic Soundtracks—helped shape the landscape of post-punk and DIY music. Now, for the first time in over 40 years, The John Peel Sessions brings together all three of their recordings for John Peel, a figure instrumental in championing their sound.

Formed in the early ’70s and fully realised by 1976, Swell Maps embodied the DIY ethos, launching their own label and self-releasing the jagged, frenetic debut single ‘Read About Seymour’ in 1978. Peel was an early supporter, playing their record as soon as it landed on his desk—a moment the band described as one of disbelief and elation. His regular airplay of their music helped solidify their cult status, and these sessions capture the raw energy, off-kilter melodies, and boundary-pushing creativity that defined them."
items._genre: post-punk / DIY punk / experimental / noise rock
items._cn_summary: Swell Maps 是1970年代末英国伯明翰的后朋克与DIY朋克代表乐队，以粗粝、混乱且具实验性的声音著称。这张合辑首次将乐队为BBC传奇DJ John Peel录制的三套现场录音完整收录，时间跨度覆盖乐队解散前最后一年。文中重点介绍了乐队成员构成（Biggles Books、Jowe Head以及Nikki Sudden与Epic Soundtracks兄弟），以及他们自主创办厂牌发行首张单曲的经历。Peel是最早支持他们的电台人物之一，这些录音保留了乐队原始的能量感、失衡的旋律线与边界突破式的创造力。作为Sonic Youth、Nirvana、R.E.M.等乐队公开承认的影响源头，Swell Maps在主流商业上从未成功，但其DIY精神与粗糙实验美学对后世独立音乐产生了深远影响。

items.body:
One of electronic music's most influential recordings, back in circulation.

Most readers of these pages will know the story, but to indulge you with a recap, Gottsching was part of electronic krautrock heroes Ash Ra Tempel and in 1981, off the back of a Klaus Schulze tour, sat down one evening and dropped a continuous piece of music which would uncannily imagine the arc of dance music for a quarter of a century.

Early adopters in the Chicago and Detroit warehouses and mediterranean pleasure palaces must have thrilled to the balanced and continuous surging flow of the hour long piece - even over two sides the mix is perfect for building a club atmosphere and suggesting avenues for mixing, whilst using merely two chords throughout. the minimalism offsets the percussive splendour perfectly - several years later the tune was rediscovered and co-opted into the huge italo house smash Sueno Latino, which cemented its foundation in the burgeoning balearic scene of the time and proceeded through several spells of rapturous revival throughout the nineties, not least when figures like Carl Craig and Basic Channel issued their own radically different reshapes and remakes of the piece.

Very satisfying then to have this Gottsching sanctioned edition, where the game might truly be said to have begun in earnest. As they say on the august walls of the Hardwax emporium - buy or die.
items._cn_summary: 这张1981年的专辑是电子音乐史上极具影响力的录音，戈特辛格在克拉斯·舒尔策巡演后的一晚即兴创作出一段持续约一小时的连续音乐作品，仅用两个和弦贯穿始终，却通过极简主义与打击乐的精妙配合构建出适合俱乐部氛围的涌动音流。该作品预示了此后二十五年的舞曲走向，早期芝加哥与底特律仓库派对以及地中海度假地的DJ们从中汲取灵感，后被改编为意大利浩室热门曲目《Sueno Latino》，并进入巴利阿里场景。九十年代卡尔·克雷格和Basic Channel等艺术家又对其进行了彻底的重新诠释。此次再版由艺术家本人授权发行，保留了原作的连贯性与混音品质，为听众提供了追溯电子舞曲源头的契机。

items.body:
Deep club modernist Sa Pa mints his own new label, Dub Techno For Life, with four top drawer cuts of textured, strident pressure tipped FFO classic Chain Reaction x Short Span.

Since 2015 Sa Pa has carved a heads-down path between techno, proper, and its conceptual adjuncts in ambient and sound designer atmospheres, most recently on Short Span and Astral Industries. Now taking matters into his own hands, the ‘Girls on Tour EP’ squares up his most robust club material alongside more experimental urges for a definitive self-portrait displaying a fine spectrum of strengths. 

The four tunes clearly speak to his diversity within a theme, checking for a firm touchstone in Andreas Tilliander aka Mokira with the 10 mins of rolling, claggy heft to ‘Mokira Ultra Dub’, unshelving his 2016 rework for deep ’26 ‘floors, alongside the puckered elegance of ‘Waiting For You’, harking to roots in Teutonic house minimalism, whereas the B-side attends to grubbier urges in the bittersweet, sludgy budge of ‘Modular System’, and lusher, abstract feels on the Actress or Rezzett-esque whorl of ‘World Saving Banger’.
items._genre: dub techno / experimental electronic / minimal / abstract beats
items._cn_summary: Sa Pa 在自创厂牌 Dub Techno For Life 推出的这张 EP 收录四首作品，介于俱乐部节奏与实验声响之间，呈现其多面向的音乐人格。'Mokira Ultra Dub' 以十分钟的厚重滚动质感呼应 Chain Reaction 时代的 dub techno 传统与 Andreas Tilliander 的极简脉络；'Waiting For You' 展现德式极简 house 的优雅克制；B 面则转向更粗粝抽象的领域，'Modular System' 以淤泥般的质感探索深沉律动，'World Saving Banger' 融入 Actress 与 Rezzett 式的朦胧抽象氛围。整体制作强调质感与空间感的塑造，模糊了 techno 俱乐部功能性与实验声响设计之间的界线，延续了 Sa Pa 自 2015 年以来在 Short Span、Astral Industries 等厂牌积累的低调探索路线。
