items.body:
Club Romantico salute an unsung pioneer of modern club movements, Daniel Pineda ov Nguzunguzu - a producer of early Kelela and the short-lived Future Brown with Fatima Al-Qadiri - with a handful of lush yet venomous originals plus a Kelman Duran link-up 

You can’t talk about the 2010’s club sound without acknowledging Daniel Pineda’s influential, border-smudging productions as half of Nguzunguzu, with Asthma Maroof. Along with the likes of Total Freedom, Pineda’s work ushered the freshest wave of syncopated club music from the US at a time when Night Slugs (and Numbers.) and its American division, Fade To Mind, were hybridising UKF with Latin house, Jersey and B-More club and a groundswell of virulent Global South rhythms that began to percolate Westwards via blogs (this was the salient stuff when talking about blog-era, not the fidget-house pish) by the end of the ‘00s. 

Pineda’s ‘Landlocked’ firmly marks his return to a scene he sowed nearly decades ago, swerving from the heart-in-mouth pads and Dutch Bubblers-type groove to ‘De La Mama’, a a slower variant of that tresillo formula in ‘Gritos’, via the full-bore 145BPM intensity of ‘Fuerte’, a video clash-meets-Ballroom romp ‘Heavy Fact’, and the pneumatic subs and drill clack of a ‘Quema’ primed for carnival season. Another crucial bridge of Global South and Western club music, Kelman Duran tags in on the EP’s slowest, heaviest, ‘Loko 4 Eva’, strapped with below-belt quake and hardest drum cadence bound to get crowds slapping the walls.

items._cn_summary: 这张EP由Club Romantico厂牌发行，向Nguzunguzu成员Daniel Pineda致敬，追溯其在2010年代美国俱乐部音乐浪潮中的开拓性贡献。专辑融合拉丁节奏、Global South律动与UK funky、Baltimore club等元素，横跨多种BPM。曲目设计呈现多样化策略：从心悬半空的和声铺垫与荷兰风格律动，到稍慢的tresillo变体；从145BPM的高强度舞曲，到video clash与Ballroom融合的凌厉节奏；再到适合狂欢季的低频冲击。Kelman Duran参与的最慢、最重曲目以极深bass与刚硬鼓组收尾。整体制作兼顾舞池实用性与文化流动性，是一座连接全球南方与西方俱乐部音乐的桥梁。

items.body:
Tighter and tidier than last year's 'Electric Chair', Cities Aviv's latest set is a psilocybin-infused dream sequence packed with fuzzy ambient interludes, loopy clouded reflections and stream-of-consciousness recitations. 

 Gavin Mays has always been on the perimeter of any given scene or other, happy enough to draw his own landscape while everyone else churns up the same mud. And that's truer than ever on his recent run; operating on his lonesome, Mays creates music that can't be pigeonholed - it's barely even rap. He spits on the two-part title track, but his words dilate awkwardly over noisy, new age-esque synths and blown-out, pitch-deformed rhythms. They might not even be strictly on the beat at all, that's not the point - Mays creates a mood that he prolongs throughout 'Even Colder Spring'. The second part of the title track sounds more like Seefeel than it does MF DOOM, anyways.

It's not always easy to digest - we'll admit we struggled with 'Spinnin & Spinnin' - but 'Even Colder Spring' is surprisingly approachable compared with many of his recent releases. And what it lacks in cohesion it more than makes up for in pure eccentricity. "Maybe Mars is bougie," he quips over electric piano arpeggios and feedback squeals on 'Tribeca', before breathing lullabies over slowed-down soul samples on 'Concrete Masks'.
items._genre: experimental hip-hop / ambient / lo-fi / cloud rap
items._cn_summary: Cities Aviv 的新作以松散的低保真质感呈现，模糊了嘻哈与实验音乐的边界。Gavin Mays 孤身运作，拒绝进入任何既有场景，人声漂浮在失真的合成器、new age 音景与变形节拍之上，刻意偏离节奏的咬字方式让作品更像氛围化的意识流独白而非传统说唱。两段式标题曲被拿来与 Seefeel 相提并论，而非 MF DOOM，暗示其更接近氛围电子而非嘻哈传统。专辑穿插电钢琴琶音、反馈噪音与慢速放大的灵魂乐采样片段，整体缺乏严密结构，却以怪异的情绪氛围取胜。'Tribeca' 中火星是否时髦的诙谐念白与 'Concrete Masks' 里摇篮曲式的说唱形成对照，展现出一种难以归类的个人美学，在抽象与可听性之间寻找平衡。

items.body:
A quiet show of strength from Chicago’s budding and already highly sought after Dub Techno specialists, Kino Disk, hustling 11 exclusive permutations of dub-suffixed ambient, techno, and elemental abstraction by label regulars and new figures including Eustress, Infant, 8004 and many others, huge tip FFO Chain Reaction, Huerco S., Echospace, Short Span, Vialan.

In the space of 20 odd releases since 2024, Kino Disk has emerged as a key point of interest for off-grid dub aficionados. ‘American Dub Electronics’ now opens an ideal entry portal to their microcosm, rendering 11 exclusive bits that speak to the label’s fine grasp of variation within a theme. Trust it’s not wall-to-wall mark & moritz worship, rather a webbed spectra of interrelated, American POV’s on the same gauzy spirit from their collected vapours.

Building on the smouldering embers of over 30 years of precedents in this field, the set sways from the moonlit tidal movement of Psalm Star Electric’s ‘001’ to the unmoored slosh of 8006 (whose ‘8004’ was a sleeper gem of ’25) with a particularly nocturnal appeal. Eustress practices the most Catholic form of dub house in the darkly luminous ‘mm’, and Eden Aurelius’ Ring impress with the ASMR-like sensitivities of ‘Changeling’, and another label regular Point Survey with the phasing dub noise of ‘Print-Through’.

Keener observers may recognise those names already, but perhaps not the new ones here, notably Corbin Cary & Taylor White’s Permutia duo, secreting the fine lather chords and sandman bassline of ‘p1.2’, or HPIN with the early SND-style puckered glitch of ‘Remote’, Uos’ washed-out textures on Uos in ‘Uos Jelly’, and dreamily poised dub waltz of ‘Speedwalker’ by a.m.p & b.p.p.
items._cn_summary: 芝加哥厂牌Kino Disk推出合辑，收录11首dub元素的电子作品，涵盖ambient、techno与抽象声响等多种变体。乐评指出该合辑并非对Basic Channel传统的简单复刻，而是以美国视角重新诠释那种朦胧绵延的精神气质——从Psalm Star Electric的潮汐律动到8006的失重质感，从Eustress的dub house暗光到Eden Aurelius的ASMR式敏感，再到Permutia的细密和弦与HPIN早期SND式的节奏故障。每位艺术家带来了dub光谱上不同的折射点，整体呈现一种夜间悬浮般的听觉氛围。厂牌自2024年以来已发行20余张作品，在地下dub领域建立了稳定的策展视角，这张合辑可视为其美学体系的入口。

items.body:
Necessary reissue of Marc Leclair’s immaculate Y2K micro-house/dub-house 12” as Akufen, dispensed by Low End Activist’s guess-again BRUK sibling to Sneaker Social Club - huge RIYL Maurizio, Studio 1, Mike Huckaby.

‘Architextures 1 -2 -3’ is a sought-after slice of hypnotic house by a noted pioneer of the micro-house movement that emerged in the late ‘90s. Its reissue arrives in the wake of a re-up for Marc Leclair’s (aka Akufen) sole solo album ‘Musique Pour 3 Femmes Enceintes’ (2005) with a strong reminder of his pivotal role in dressing house music down to fundamentals around the millennium, as deployed in Richie Hawtin mixes and praised for its exquisitely efficient, effortless, hiccuping funk.

It’s really all about the  A-side’s ‘Architexture 1’, a pendulous 127BPM roller inflected with chef’s kiss dub chords and frisky drums, on one of the smoothest, deepest basslines since ‘M5’. There’s a good reason why it’s been fetching triple figures on 2nd hand markets, so BRUK are doing the Lord’s work with this reissue, which also includes the slower, sub-heavier swivel of its Pt. 2, and more signature, strutting clip of his tight sampling tekkerz on Pt. 3.

TIP!
items._genre: micro-house / dub-house / minimal techno / deep house
items._cn_summary: Akufen（本名Marc Leclair）的《Architextures 1-2-3》Y2K时期微型浩室经典12寸再版，由独立厂牌BRUK发行。文章聚焦A面Architexture 1：127BPM的催眠律动搭载dub和弦、轻盈碎鼓与深沉贝斯线，被比作Maurizio经典曲目《M5》以降最丝滑的低频质感之一。整张EP展现了Akufen以极简采样技法将浩室解构为基本元素的手法，曾影响Richie Hawtin等DJ的混音选曲。Pt.2延续更慢更沉的变体，Pt.3则呈现招牌式的紧凑采样律动。作为千禧年前后微型浩室运动的重要先驱，此作在二级市场曾以三位数价格流通，本次再版具有相当收藏与聆听价值。

items.body:
Limited edition, first time 2LP re-issue of a compilation originally released via Gary Mundy's legendary Broken Flag imprint in 1987 and featuring a veritable who’s who of post industrial drone and psyche/power electronics including Ramleh, Total, Andrew Chalk and many more.​

"Remastered by Puppy38, this features two bonus tracks not included on the original (and long o/p) LP but only previously found on the even rarer cassette and the equally o/p CD. A timely reminder of this fantastic archive document full of boundary-pushing artists mostly still active in one form or another. Packaged in a sleeve faithful to the distinctive original Cranioclast-designed cover."
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑是1987年Broken Flag厂牌发行的经典作品的首次2LP再版限量版本，汇集了Ramleh、Total、Andrew Chalk等多位后工业音乐与嗡鸣/力量电子领域的核心人物。专辑由Puppy38重新母带处理，并收录了两首原本仅在稀有磁带与CD版本中出现的bonus曲目。内容侧重于噪音墙、嗡鸣质感与极端声响的探索，跨越了工业、实验与心理声学的边界。封面由Cranioclast设计，保留了原版独特的视觉风格。文本偏重发行信息介绍，对具体音乐内容的描述较为有限，但合辑涉及的艺术家群体与厂牌背景指向了地下实验场景的核心脉络。

items.body: Adrift, by Pleq and Hakobune, has been given the reissue treatment. Remastered by Ian Hawgood, Adrift’s sound has further opened thanks to its original masters making the transition to reel-to-reel. The NKR release, which came out in 2012, has now found a place on Home Normal, and this newly-packaged edition also features remixes from Olan Mill, offthesky, and Polar M. Giulio Aldinucci provides the panoramic cover art, which fits the open and windswept music down to a T. Adrift’s ambient music is mesmeric and its immersive soundscapes are left open to individual interpretation. One would expect nothing less than a stellar album from these two experienced musicians, especially when the music fits so snugly within the ambient field, but the transfer to reel-to-reel has opened up another dimension in which the music can enter and engage with the listener in new and striking ways. Like an upgrade to High Definition or tapping into 4k resolution for the first time, this reissue opens the ambient floodgates and brings new life into its eight-year-old music…not that it felt dated. Everything is refreshed and brought into a new decade, but this reissue also highlights the fact that the original record was quality, as it hasn’t really aged at all. If anything, it feels younger than ever before. After a lengthy opener, title track ‘Adrift’ adds recurring ambient swells which fall into regular, tidal rhythms which could either recall the sea or the repeated sway of branches and leaves on a windy day, passing through and over the trees. The music rises in volume and then falls back, while field recordings of birdsong are clustered in the background, adding to the sense of the great outdoors. The listener could be adrift in both worlds, on land or at sea, in a wooded area, deep in the forest, or afloat on the ocean. At sixteen minutes, ‘Horizon Line’ has plenty of time for development, and this leads to a deeper, immersive experience. The track fluctuates with its water-like, fluid tones while an array of loose, light textures sporadically emerge, and a stronger, resolute drone hovers at the forefront. Closer ’The Land Unknown’ adds an element of mystery to the record. Here, the exotic sound of a rainforest, teeming with life, blends in with a darker, tribal drone to create a fascinating track. The rainforest’s abundant lifeforms can represent Adrift as a whole, because its transfer to reel-to-reel has paradoxically sharpened the music and given it an extra life. Life flows through the record, turning everything it touches into a new creation while retaining some semblance of its eight-year-old self. Even if the notes and textures appear to be the same, the appearance of the music has changed, looking fresher and more tranquil, and its resulting music has more flesh on its bones. Whichever way you look at it, Adrift is a welcome reissue for an impressive release, and one which is keen to explore new continents instead of treading over the same old ground. Adrift (Remastered + Remixed) by Pleq & Hakobune www.homenormal.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: Pleq与Hakobune合作的专辑《Adrift》经重新母带处理后由Home Normal厂牌再版发行。原版2012年由NKR发行，本次再版经Ian Hawgood将原始母带转至开盘磁带进行重新制作，使声场进一步打开。专辑收录了Olan Mill、offthesky与Polar M的混音版本，封面由Giulio Aldinucci操刀。音乐以环境氛围与无人机为核心，长篇曲目如十六分钟的《Horizon Line》展现了流水般的音色起伏与松散质感的层叠铺陈；《The Land Unknown》则融入热带雨林田野录音与部落感无人机音色，营造异域氛围。再版通过开盘磁带媒介的转换，使原有音色获得新生，细节更鲜活、空间感更开阔，整张专辑呈现出自然、开阔且沉浸的声音景观。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items._genre: world music / Afro-Portuguese fusion / 70s-80s African sounds
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了圣多美和普林西比这两个非洲小岛在七十至八十年代录制的音乐，风格被称为Puxa，融合了来自其他葡语非洲殖民地的节奏元素，同时吸收了merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等加勒比海沿岸的律动。乐评指出，尽管两地只有十二个村庄，却产出了超出当地人口规模的丰富音乐场景——录音稀缺只是因为缺乏像拉各斯或内罗毕那样的城市录音产业基础。合辑以Pedro Lima领衔的乐队为代表，展现多把吉他交织缠绕、人声与器乐呼应的编制特征，部分曲目在贝斯与键盘退场后仅靠鼓与吉他推进律动，被描述为能让舞者陷入狂热的状态。乐评也强调这些岛屿独立于外部影响的本土特质，使Puxa在各种外来元素中仍保留自身识别度。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items._genre: experimental folk / avant-garde / drone / contemporary classical
items._cn_summary: Alison Cotton的新专辑以中提琴、簧风琴、击弦古钢琴和钢琴为核心乐器，部分曲目加入鼓、贝斯和合成器，大部分音乐采用即兴方式一次性录制完成。整体风格介于民俗、前卫与宗教音乐之间，融合中世纪圣咏般的开篇与缓慢级联的钢琴旋律，并辅以持续的嗡鸣低音铺垫。专辑是对Cotton已故父亲的纪念之作，弥漫着失去亲人的哀愁与温柔，光与暗在不同曲目中交替流转。评论特别提到John Clare的诗作被设置为超脱尘世的曲调，以及被形容为'完美珍珠'的中心曲《Sprigs of Heather》。音乐拒绝被简单归类，在挑战与抚慰之间寻找平衡。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.
Tiny Sun -
Vanishment
(Review)
Carolina Chocolate Drops -
Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)
items.label: Buda Musique
items._genre: bal-musette / ragtime / jug band / French chanson / skiffle
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源于Dominique Cravic与漫画家Robert Crumb在1986年的构想，他们从旧78转唱片中挖掘被遗忘的曲目，用手风琴、萨克斯、木琴、单簧管、班卓琴、尤克里里、特雷门、夏威夷吉他等杂糅乐器重新演绎。27首短曲以Cravic近似平民Maurice Chevalier的说唱方式为主，在法式小酒馆音乐基底上杂糅多种历史风格，既包含对Juliette Gréco的致敬，也覆盖《Smoke Gets in Your Eyes》《Take Five》等经典旋律。乐评强调其难以归类，但演奏者以严肃态度和十足投入赋予老音乐新的活力，类似Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks的不可定义气质。专辑以好奇心和档案式考据驱动，在复古外壳下呈现独特的艺术视角，值得一听。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: Camilla Hole Trio在《Langs》中将挪威西部传统民间旋律与爵士即兴语言结合。主奏乐器为高音萨克斯，与贝斯和鼓构成灵活的声部配置。乐评以开篇曲《Springleik》为例展开分析，该曲源自挪威西部的传统舞蹈旋律。三人组合的特点在于角色不固定，乐器之间的旋律主导权频繁流转。贝斯手Kalman先以模块合成器与打击乐提供节奏底色，随后接手旋律与Hole齐奏；鼓手Nesheim则在后半段拓展节奏维度。Hole以高音萨克斯重新呈现旋律动机，三重奏在固定主题与开放即兴之间不断切换。相较前作《Eventyrferd》中科幻合成器音色与民谣素材的大胆嫁接，《Langs》回归更接近地面的声音处理，但依然延续对北欧民间音乐边界之外素材的探索。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary / sound art
items._cn_summary: 这不是传统意义上的音乐作品，而是由录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区街头采集的田野录音项目。25位枪支暴力幸存者参与其中，年龄从17岁到67岁不等，录制地点位于一位94岁祖母家的前廊，正值特朗普下令向该市部署国民警卫队的当天。专辑完全不使用配乐，所有声音均为现场真实环境音，偶尔穿插自由说唱。一位失去两个儿子的年长女性在讲述过程中情绪崩溃，反复道歉，而编辑明确指出社会才应该是道歉的一方。参与者既包括暴力施加者也包括承受者，几乎社区中每个人都与暴力有某种关联。项目收益将捐赠给致力于以公共卫生方法终结暴力的Cure Violence Global组织。整体呈现出强烈的社会纪实色彩与声音艺术理念的结合。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — WARNING: This is a release of material recorded in 1972 that represents two different bands containing some of the same musicians that just happen to overlap in that year.Recorded 1972, unreleased until 1999. I was turned on to Riff Raff a few weeks ago so I've been slowly getting to know their music and their story. I was immediately impressed (and astounded that I'd never heard of them--even in my 18 years associated with ProgArchives) by all of their albums--which made the decision of which album to review first very difficult since, in learning their story I'd discovered that their first records--their debut album--had never been released at the time of its creation. But I do like to get to know a band/artist in chronological order if I can, so, of course I want to start with their first album: the problem is that their first album that became known to the public was their second album, the eponymously titled Riff Raff from 1973; Outside Looking In never reached public ears until 1999! As I've been listening to this album I've come to know that the opening 39 minutes represent material performed by the band's original lineup, a project calling themselves, STRABISMUS, which recorded this material in London in 1972. The second 23-minutes of "Bonus Tracks" represents Roger Sutton and Tommy Eyre's more-Jazz-oriented band, RIFF RAFF. Sutton, himself a former member of Brian Auger's Trinity project, continued to develop Riff Raff for the next few years with keyboardist Tommy Eyre, guitarist Peter Kirtley, and drummer Aureo De Souza before giving himself completely to Ian Carr's NUCLEUS. Peter Kirtley's most notable credit post-Riff Raff was his contribution to an album that has always remained dear to me: Yes' Alan White's first solo album, 1976's Ramshackled., while also joining The Pentangle during their tenure in the 1990s. Tommy Eyre himself was a product of previous collaborations with Aynsley Dunbar and Mark-Almond. He would go on to make significant contributions to successful albums by Zzebra, Alex Harvey, Gerry Rafferty, Gary Moore, John Martyn, Greg Lake, Michael Schenker, and Wham!. Singer Alan Marshall was hired by Zzebra (at the suggestion of the band's newcomer keyboard player, Tommy Eyre) as their singer for the 1974-75 sessions and tour that would produce the material for the band's classic sophomore album, Panic, as well as a third and fourth album--which weren't released until 1999 and 2001, respectively. Brasilian-born percussionist/drummer Aureo De Souza would also find himself hired by Ian Carr, as a percussionist, for Nucleus' mid-70s classic funk albums, but the material he recorded with the band never reached the public as part of their studio album releases--only surfaced years later (mostly in the 21st Century) when record labels Vertigo, Andy Gray's BGO (Beat Goes On) Records, and Esoteric Recordings began releasing retrospective CDs that included outtakes and live performances.Line-up / Musicians:As STRABISMUS:- Alan Marshall / vocals- Martin Ball / guitar- Tommy Eyre / Hammond organ, keyboards, acoustic guitar- Richie Dalton / saxophone- Roger Sutton (Brian Auger's Trinity) / bass, acoustic guitars, vocals- Rob Coombes (Juicy Lucy, Stealers Wheel) / drums, percussion & acoustic guitar- Joe Peters (Jackie Jocko) / drumsAs RIFF RAFF:- Alan Marshall / vocals- Peter Kirtley / guitar- Kenny Slade (Joe Cocker) / drums- Aureo De Souza / drums, percussion- Tommy Eyre / Hammond organ, keyboards, acoustic guitar- Richie Dalton / saxophone- Roger Sutton / bass, acoustic guitars, vocals(As Strabismus):1. "Outside Looking In" (9:12) opening a debut album with a long-playing jam is bold and brave! I guess it lets the listener know what kind of band they thought of themselves (unless the song order was altered over time or never decided at the time of its first creation): not hit makers. The material here is heavy, fully Rock 'n' Roll with some creative touches, nice construction and delivery, more akin to hard rockin' guitar-jammin' bands like Cream, Spirit, Mountain, Humble Pie, etc. (18.125/20)2. "The Blind Man" (8:16) opens with a much more acoustic orientation: bluesy piano, percussion and drums, Hammond organ, acoustic guitars, and vocals from a gravelly-voiced male singer. I'm immediately reminded of Southern Rock bands like The Allman Brothers and The Marshall Tucker Band. The cessation of the vocal leads into a rockin' jam with saxophonist Richie Dalton really letting loose with some wild screaming sounds. But then there is this totally unexpected transition around the five-minute mark into a more delicate, almost folk-Mexican acoustic guitar motif in which I believe four of the band members drop their instruments to pick up acoustic guitars and then what sounds like professional choral singers join in singing "Close your eyes, I can feel you" over and over before Alan rejoins to sing over them to the song's close. Very cool and unexpected song and music. (18.25/20)3. "Bach B. Minor Prelude" (2:58) a full solo on a church organ! Luscious! Another very cool and unexpected song. (9/10)4. "Feeling Paranoic" (0:43) a theatric song that feels like an outtake from Judas' or Jesus' performances in Jesus Christ Superstar. (4.375/5)5. "Buthelezi" (3:42) drummer Joe Peters leads the way through a drum & percussion jam that involves Rob Coombes and others. I love this kind of stuff--especially in live performances (or to participate in) but I'm not sure of its place on a studio album: it seems as if this space could/should have been given to a proper full-band song composition. But then I'm beginning to wonder if there is a conceptual theme, intention, or organization to the album. Anyone? (9/10)6. "So You Want To Be Free" (10:52) the music here is a return to the raw hard rock that we encountered with the album's opening song, "Outside Looking In." The raw, gravelly voice of Alan Marshall is back up front for the first couple minutes, then the music transitions into a vamp governed by a quick three-note riff that is repeated over and over while everyone just jams over and around it: saxophone, electric piano, drums, even, eventually, electric guitar. The sax solo is the best of the three; guitarist Martin Ball is not "fully formed" yet though he does sound better once the vamp slows down and punctuates itself like some Swamp Blues and he starts shredding for speed. (I guess he needed to get warmed up.) Martin's solo section ends with some well-timed whole-band chord bashing which sounds really cool and inventive--like something King Crimsonian--but then the music turns to smoother blues rock over which two male vocalists sing, gentler, harmonizing, before the music begins to slowly devolve into just a few percussion/cymbal noises and guitar and electric piano notes. Brilliant--and so creative! (18.25/20)7. "Changes" (3:23) acoustic guitar accompanying Alan's singing on what sounds like a cover but apparently is just another of the album's Sutton/Coombes compositions. Simple and nice; definitely could have been developed into something bigger. (8.667/10)Total time: 39:06A-/4.5 stars; a near-masterpiece of eclectic Southern Power Rock.Bonus Tracks (as Riff Raff):8. "Child Of The Summer" (5:59) a jazzy feeling song with a syncopated, complex construction and feeling vocal performance (reminiscent of Allan's performance on Allan White's Ramshakled). After the chorus the band revs up and becomes more rock-forceful--but it's still good! Nice wah-wah-ed electric guitar work, great background vocal work, great dirty electric piano, and awesome bass, drums, and percussion at the base. This is the rock-perspective to Jazz-Rock Fusion that I've been hoping to find more of! (9.25/10)9. "For Every Dog" (4:05) a truly awesome acoustic Southern Rock song that should/could've been a radio-friendly hit back in 1973. Great weave of instrumental performances blessed with a weave of awesome group harmonized vocals. Shades of The Youngbloods, Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young, Ozark Mountain Daredevils, Pure Prairie League, or the early Doobie Brothers or Eagles. (9.5/10)10. "Morning" (5:57) piano-based soft bluesy light folk/Americana pop arranged with an odd triple-hop at the end of each measure. The singer is mostly backed by another harmonizing vocalist (or vocal track) while acoustic guitars, bass, and gentle drums back/accompany the piano and singers. I believe a flute may also be in the mix though its replication of the piano's legato may be just be a second piano track. A very pleasant, not-quite-Cat Stevens, not-quite-Harry Nilsson tune. (8.875/10) 11. "The Garden" (6:59) bluesy solo piano opens this for about 30 seconds before Allan and the background choir vocalists join in. The song sounds almost like a church/liturgical piece--something one might hear in the countryside villages of Ireland. Strummed 12-string acoustic guitar, bass, congas, and drums slowly, almost surreptitiously, join in as Allan gives his hear and soul to his vocal performance. There is definitely a flute in this one--entering just before the piano ramps things up with more volume. There is a little Dave Mason "We Just Disagree" sound and feel here. Then Allan really brings it: belting out with two minutes to go but then things quickly de-escalate as he and his backing singers sing softly about the importance of our ancestor/elders. It drags on a bit but it's a very nice song with a great vocal performance and some nice, positive lyrics. (13.375/15)Total time: 24:00A-/five stars; a minor masterpiece of Jazz- and Rock-informed Southern Folk Rock.Total Time: 62:06 I don't usually review "bonus" material in my album reviews (because I want to treat the material as it would have been heard in the year it was recorded) but then when this was (finally) released in 1999 it arrived in CD format and, thus, being its first exposure to the public, should be heard as a whole. The problem, of course, comes with the fact that the material is really the result of two completely different bands: one that never really persisted, the other which came out and toured for a year or so before scattering its members across the musical spectrum in the UK and US. I definitely like both "albums" though the Riff Raff "bonus" material is more of the kind of stuff that I'd listen to over and over. (I almost want to rate the two "albums" separately! A-/five stars; a minor masterpiece of Jazz-infused Southern Folk Rock.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了1972年录制、直到1999年才公开的素材，前39分钟来自原始阵容乐队Strabismus，后23分钟为Riff Raff乐队的爵士化探索曲目。乐评重点并非音乐本身的技术分析，而是梳理乐队成员的历史脉络与错综复杂的人物关系网络——吉他手Peter Kirtley后来参与Alan White首张专辑，键盘手Tommy Eyre辗转于Zzebra、Wham!等多支乐队，鼓手Aureo De Souza则加入了Ian Carr的Nucleus。这篇文字更像是一篇音乐考古笔记而非传统乐评，详细记录了这些1970年代英国爵士摇滚场景中音乐人的协作轨迹与后续发展。作为ProgArchives的评论，文章信息密度较高，但缺乏对实际演奏、编曲特点与音响质感的深入探讨，偏向历史考据而非艺术评价。对于关注爵士摇滚史和英国前卫音乐场景的听众而言具有一定参考价值。

items.body: Canadian netlabel Panospria released “I-II-III”, the debut album under the Silver Shadow name, on 15 July 2026. It runs to 26 tracks across three volumes gathered into a single digital set, sold in MP3 and FLAC from 15 Canadian dollars, and it moves between IDM, ambient, drone and minimal techno. The release page presents the album as three distinct volumes compiled into one, and as the latest work of a long-standing name on the label. It never prints that name: “Having recently relocated to France from Canada, keen listeners will surely deduce the identity of this mainstay on our label. New country, new alias, new directions in music.” The label’s own announcement is less coy than the release page. It presents Silver Shadow as the new alias of the artist formerly recording as Silent Q and Gyges. Both of those names belong to Paul Keeley, a Montreal electronic producer whose Gyges album “Composite Massive” was Panospria’s second release in 2004 and who has issued deep and progressive house under his own name through Thinner, Epsilonlab and Anjunadeep. The Silver Shadow Bandcamp page gives the artist’s location as Paris. What is on the Silver Shadow album ‘I-II-III’ The three volumes are not new to the same degree. Volume I is the eight-track album “I”, put on Bandcamp on 26 July 2022, and volume II is the ten-track “II” from 22 November 2024; the remaining eight tracks, from “Delores” to “Matte”, appear here for the first time. II by Silver Shadow Track titles run as compressed fragments throughout: “Aieesqvb96”, “nFU-VHToT”, “HshShsHs”, “HpnoTod”, “Grgwld”, “Dickenszs”. In order the album reads Aieesqvb96, Fulter, Plyurs, nFU-VHToT, Crunge, Duke, Spong, Purf, Ghosnen, AmbWks, Mmoonn, TheLab, Pull, HshShsHs, HpnoTod, Unstld, Grgwld, Roogah, Delores, KiBC8, NewWav, Sheets, Dickenszs, Krud, Thumb and Matte. About Silver Shadow and Panospria Silver Shadow first appeared on Bandcamp on 3 April 2020 with the five-track “A”, followed by “I” in 2022 and “II” in 2024, so the Panospria set is a label debut rather than a first release under the alias. Panospria itself grew out of the Canadian prairies around the turn of the millennium and put out its first offering, the “Alphaform” compilation, in 2002 with Dublin’s Psychonavigation. The label was properly established in Montreal that same year and was among the earliest to treat the MP3 as a release format in its own right. It moved with its operators, running from Montreal until 2008, then Vancouver, then Saskatoon from 2022. Alongside the catalogue it ran two concert series: Textures in Montreal and Quiet City in Vancouver, the latter reaching 70 editions over a decade. In 2007 the Panospria catalogue was folded into the Montreal netlabel No Type, which has been active since 1998 and also runs Annexe, BricoLodge, Nishi and Sine Fiction; Panospria has operated as a No Type sublabel since. Paul Keeley’s connection to the label goes back almost to the start. The Gyges record “Composite Massive” carried the second catalogue number in 2004, and he has since appeared on Panospria releases by Heart & Soul, Shoebomber, Arnau Sala and N4K3D D1G1TS. “I-II-III” is the first Silver Shadow release Panospria has issued, and by the label’s account the first since the move from Canada to France.

items.body: On “Londi”, a guitar follows a kora so closely you could take the two for one instrument. The kora is Sura Susso‘s, a Gambian raised in a griot family and long settled in London; the guitar is Habib Koité‘s, the Malian who tunes to a pentatonic scale and works the open strings until it sings in the kora’s register. Londi is the Mandinka word for knowledge, and Susso sings it in Mandinka and Wolof as a tribute to the djeli, the West African storytellers and historians who carry a people’s memory in performance rather than on the page. Both musicians were born to it, Koité into a noble line of Khassonké griots, Susso into a Gambian kora dynasty. The single opens Londi, a record a decade in the making. Susso and Koité met in 2016, when promoter and label African Night Fever, showcasing African music in the Brighton Area, brought Koité to Britain and put Susso on as support, and the nightly improvising that followed grew first into a friendship and then into an album. Half of it was cut in Bamako with Koité, the rest in Banjul with Susso’s band. It arrives on 9 October as African Night Fever’s debut release, with Gambian kora player Jaliba Kuyateh guesting on another track, “Yamaro”. From the studio it moves to the stage: the Manding Melody tour carries the project across nine UK dates between 22 October and 1 November, Susso leading a cross-generational band from Senegal, Mali and The Gambia, built around kora, balafon, percussion and bass. “Londi” came out as a single on 14 August. Stream “Londi” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Habib Koité & Sura Susso – Londi appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items._cn_summary: 《Londi》是马里吉他手Habib Koité与冈比亚科拉琴演奏家Sura Susso历时十年打磨的合作专辑，以Mandinka语中意为"知识"的Londi为题，向承载西非口述传统的djeli（格里奥）致敬。Koité出身Khassonké贵族格里奥世家，调弦至五声音阶后让开放弦模仿科拉琴的音色；Susso则来自冈比亚科拉琴世家。两人2016年在英国Brighton演出中相遇，每晚即兴催生了友谊并最终凝结为此作。专辑半部分在巴马科录制，半部分在班珠尔完成，冈比亚科拉琴家Jaliba Kuyateh亦客串。制作方African Night Fever同时启动Manding Melody巡演，横跨英国九城，乐阵容纳塞内加尔、马里与冈比亚三地乐手。整体呈现跨地域格里奥传统与器乐对话的融合质地。

items.body: Sarah Davachi The Will of Tongues Performer-composer Sarah Davachi delivers a culminating body of work for organ, ensemble and choir which rewards deep listening The Will of Tongues by Sarah Davachi The Will of Tongues, the latest record by performer-composer Sarah Davachi, is a marvel of time. The record draws on Davachi’s many years of engagement with historical instruments and fascination with various tuning systems, textures and harmonic structures, featuring reconstructed period wind instruments, historically tuned organs and an abstracted Renaissance choral form. It also makes excellent use of the centuries of combined musical experience brought to bear by her many collaborators, most of whom are noted performer-composers themselves (Whitney Johnson, Eyvind Kang, and Lucy Railton among them). And then there’s the two-hour-plus runtime. Taken... The post Sarah Davachi – The Will of Tongues appeared first on The Quietus.

items._cn_summary: Sarah Davachi 的《The Will of Tongues》是一张围绕管风琴、室内乐及合唱团构建的长篇作品，融合了历史乐器、复调调律体系与抽象化的文艺复兴合唱形式。专辑以两小时以上的时长铺陈时间感与和声纹理，邀请听众进行深度聆听。她邀请了多位身兼演奏家与作曲家的合作者参与录制，集合了多种历史管乐器的重建版本与特殊调律的管风琴音色。整张作品在缓慢展开的声学空间中探索音色分层与共振效果，体现了对古老音乐传统的当代重新诠释，是一部强调空间感与历史质感的实验性当代古典作品。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — One of those Renaissance men that could have found success in many (any?) careers, this album was Volker's debut as a band leader. After stints with Ingfreid Hoffmann and Klaus Doldinger in the mid-60s, for With a Little Help from My Friends we find the creative guitarist working with some of the same musicians that he worked with on Klaus Doldinger's Goes On album while also working with drummer Peter Baumeister for the first time. Tracks A1 to A4 were recorded in 1968 in K�ln while Tracks B1 to B3 were recorded in 1968 in Frankfurt. The album was then released by Liberty Records, also sometime in 1968. ‎A1. "With A Little Help From My Friends" (3:13) though quite faithful to the Beatles' original vocal melody lines, Volker is so accurate and precise as to almost seem reverential (i.e., not the creative Jazz treatment I was expecting). (8.875/10)A2. "Blues For Instance" (5:10) definitely built/based on American Blues construct and melodies, Volker, bassist Peter Trunk, and drummer Cees See give ample life to this original composition. Not my favorite type of music, but the trio really bring their best to make it both interesting and impressive. (8.75/10)A3. "Norwegian Wood" (2:20) now this is more of what I was expecting from Volker's first tackle of a Lennon & McCartney tune: creative interpretation, juxtaposition, variation, and improvisation galore; he's using the original as a jumping off point, not as a template to follow respectfully close. The injections of Jazz twists and turns are rampant and replete--and nary a sitar or sitar-imitation necessary! (9/10)A4. "Traffic Jam" (3:59) the fourth and final song from the K�ln studio recording sessions finds Volker stretching out with his band on this original composition that is founded in more of a folk Jazz tradition similar to the works of Django Rheinhard but Volker finds his usual ways of making it his own: expanding Django-like phrasing into American Jazz traditions pioneered by Charlie Christian as well as sneaking in a some flourishes of psychedelic rock into the last minute of the song. This, to my mind, is the first song that really begins to show Volker's wildly creative genius in tandem with his virtuosic dexterity. I really like drummer Cees See's instinctual sensibilities and control when he fully joins in around the halfway mark. (8.875/10)B1. "Morandi" (3:29) another Kriegel original that finds Volker exploring the sounds and styles of Spanish classical guitaring of Rodrigo, Segovia, Ni�o Ricardo, and Manolo Sanl�car. Most people think of Volker as an electric guitarist but I'm here to tell you that he was an amazing acoustic guitarist as well. As I suggested in this review's introductory paragraph, I consider Volker quite the eclectic musician: a Zelig who could and would transgress fearlessly into any style or genre of sound or music with an ease that I credit to intuition as much as to intention--and the dude was totally self-taught! (9.125/10)B2. "Na Na Imboro" (8:42) a composition from Claudio Szenkar, the Vibraphonist sitting in on all of the songs on Side Two (those songs recorded in Frankfurt). The main melody and structure have quite a similar feel to the song "Mas Que Nada" (made famous internationally in 1966 by Sergio Mendes & Brasil '66). While Peter Baumeister flails away with great vim and vigor, bassist G�nter Lenz keeps up as Claudio and Volker trade vibrant and dynamic solos, both challenging the other to up their game, even urging the other on from beneath the soloist's spotlight while the other is soloing! Very cool and energetic Jazz! Virtuosi, both! (18.625/20)B3. "Interpunctuation" (4:44) though Claudio and Volker lay down the chords, this song presents itself as more of a vehicle to show off the drumming talents of Peter Baumeister. After the first minute, though, Peter and G�nter settle into something structured while Volker nad Claudio take turns soloing, Volker riffing with such smooth fluidity as to surprise and astonish, over and over again. Claudio uses his genius to show his chord play during his solo (toward the end). I kind of wish Peter's drums were mixed a little more quietly into the final mix: they can be a little overbearing. (9.125/10)Total time 31:37Though for whatever reason I find myself resistant to listening to Volker Kriegel material, I always come away super impressed by this musician's abilities. He attacks the guitar with such intuition and virtuosity and yet he somehow makes it sound so easy! There are other fluid guitarists out there but I can think of no other who makes his fluid movements and clear note play seem as effortless as Volker--even here, at age 25, in this, his first record as a bandleader. And then there's the factor of his compositional abilities: these four original compositions of his are so good, so complete, and so confident, that it makes the listener swear that they must be covers of old classic songs by much more mature and practiced composers! A-/five stars; a minor masterpiece of proto-Jazz-Rock Fusion: here fusing jazz interpretations of a variety of musics (Pop, Spanish, American Blues, and Brasilian) with eclectic meanderings from his encyclopedic mind. Brilliant! Volker is a force! And I need to hear more of Claudio Szenkar's work!
items._genre: jazz fusion / jazz rock / progressive jazz
items._cn_summary: 这张1968年的首张专辑展现了吉他手Volker Kriegel作为乐队领袖的多元风格尝试。专辑前半部分在科隆录制，包含对披头士歌曲的爵士化改编——《Norwegian Wood》以即兴变奏和爵士转折处理原作旋律，而《Traffic Jam》则从Django Reinhardt的吉普赛爵士传统出发，融入Charlie Christian式的美式爵士语汇与迷幻摇滚元素。专辑后半部分在法兰克福录制，《Morandi》探索西班牙古典吉他传统，借鉴Rodrigo与Segovia的手法。Kriegel作为自学成才的音乐人，在电吉他与原声吉他之间自如切换，将蓝调、民谣爵士、古典吉他与迷幻摇滚熔于一炉。彼得·特朗克与Cees See等乐手的配合也为作品提供了灵活的三重奏框架。尽管整体仍偏向爵士摇滚融合范畴，但其跨风格实验的广度与早期爵士摇滚的探索精神对理解该流派的演变有一定参考价值。

items.body: There comes a point, after enough headlines, alerts, feeds, clips, corrections, denials, cropped videos, expert panels, anonymous sources, and professional faces staring gravely into cameras, when information begins to resemble an industrial solvent poured directly onto the brain. Reality remains somewhere underneath, presumably, but reaching it requires digging through so many layers of interpretation that certainty starts feeling less like knowledge than another product somebody is trying to sell. Baltimore electro-industrial duo Pygmy Children, brothers Pete and Brian Roper, plant Proof in Lies directly inside that psychic mess. The track leads their forthcoming fifth studio album, Into The Silence. The music carries the physical force of industrial rock without turning itself into machinery: drums strike with hard, deliberate weight, guitars grind against serrated electronics, and Pete Roper delivers his vocals from somewhere between accusation, exhaustion, and the suspicion that everyone in the room has already agreed upon the wrong version of events. Nine Inch Nails, Ministry, Christian Death, and the severe electronic rock of later Gary Numan all come to mind, although Pygmy Children funnel those affinities through their own Baltimore-bred sense of unease. “I rediscovered some old lyrics in a notebook for a track that had never fully materialized,” says Pete Roper. “I still remembered the original chord progression, so I rewrote the lyrics, recorded the initial drum tracks, and the project began to take shape.” That resurrection feels appropriate for a song preoccupied with evidence, memory, and the slippery authority of whatever appears before our eyes. Proof in Lies examines a culture in which perception competes continuously with experience, while repetition can make the grotesque seem ordinary and the ridiculous seem plausible. Once violence becomes entertainment, catastrophe becomes content, and human suffering becomes another image between advertisements, the ability to distinguish participation from spectatorship begins to rot. Roper ultimately locates his remaining point of orientation in music, describing it as a place of clarity, peace, and honest expression. That conviction gives the track an emotional center beneath its metal-edged pressure: somewhere behind all the competing signals remains the stubborn belief that expression can still communicate something uncorrupted. The accompanying video pushes the idea further through live performance footage, original visual effects, and public-domain animation produced during the 1940s, recombined into an uneasy collision of obedience, fantasy, violence, and entertainment. “The imagery in the video challenges our blurred perception of the boundary between reality and fantasy as we move through life increasingly disconnected from one another, following established paths without question and becoming desensitized to experiences beyond ourselves. The social acceptance of violence as a form of entertainment also emerges as a recurring theme. Finally, the unanswered question of what the recurring mysterious character possesses invites deeper interpretation.” Watch below: By the end, Proof in Lies leaves certainty battered beyond recognition, which may be the most accurate portrait possible of an age where everybody has access to everything and somehow nobody can agree on what they have seen. Listen to Proof In Lies below and order the single here, out now via Re:Mission Entertainment. items._cn_summary: Pygmy Children 是来自巴尔的摩的二人组，由兄弟 Pete 和 Brian Roper 组成，新单曲《Proof in Lies》领衔他们的第五张录音室专辑《Into The Silence》。作品直面当代信息过载与认知失序的命题，鼓击沉重而克制，吉他与锯齿状电子音色相互摩擦，主唱人声介于指控与疲惫之间。编曲参考了 Nine Inch Nails、Ministry、Christian Death 及 Gary Numan 后期作品，但融入了自身巴尔的摩式的阴郁气质。歌词源于 Pete Roper 从旧笔记本中重新发掘的未完成作品，围绕证据、记忆与视觉权威的滑移展开探讨。配套 MV 将现场演出影像、原创视觉特效与1940年代公共领域动画拼贴重组，呈现服从、幻想、暴力与娱乐的碰撞。音乐被 Roper 视为喧嚣中残存的清晰之地，为金属质感的外壳提供了情感支点。

items.body: Grief has a strange relationship with distance. The dead may be unreachable in any practical sense, yet the mind keeps inventing routes toward them: dreams, remembered voices, photographs, coincidences that briefly acquire the weight of messages. Frankie Rose describes that nocturnal search with the rueful humour of someone who knows how unreliable the equipment can be. Her latest single, Return To Dust, has intense emotional gravity. Drawn from Rose’s forthcoming album Hila, the song treats grief as a condition in which perception grows unstable, opening possibilities that daylight tends to dismiss. Rose’s voice hangs high in the arrangement, cool and clear against drums and synthesizers with considerable physical force beneath them. There are echoes of Enya’s suspended grandeur, PJ Harvey’s severity, the private ache of Cat Power, and the voluptuous gloom of Portishead; elsewhere, the guitar and vocal textures recall Cocteau Twins and the ceremonial grandeur of Siouxsie and the Banshees. Rose has spent much of the past fifteen years refining her ability to make scale and solitude coexist. On Return To Dust, enormous spaces seem to open around a voice that remains remarkably intimate. The production has breadth without sacrificing detail, with each layer contributing to an impression of drifting farther from familiar coordinates while carrying something painfully terrestrial along for the ride. “In my dreams I travel the cosmos and the astral realm looking for ones I’ve lost,” says Frankie Rose. “But I’m a pretty bad receiver, and I am pretty sure I keep missing what they’re trying to tell me.” The self-directed video literalizes Rose’s celestial preoccupations with a playful montage that sends her wandering through the cosmos. She floats among stars and planetary vistas, appearing less like an astronaut conquering unknown territory than a traveller amusing herself while attempting an impossible form of correspondence. The homemade theatricality is crucial. Rather than turning bereavement into solemn science fiction, Rose permits herself whimsy, introducing the peculiar comedy of trying to locate the dead somewhere beyond the visible universe. The video’s cosmic scenery therefore feels less like escape than an extension of mourning itself. Loss can make ordinary reality seem insufficient, sending the imagination searching for some hidden frequency on which absence might become communication. Rose understands the absurdity in that desire and allows it to remain absurd without diminishing its emotional force. Somewhere beyond the planets, perhaps, a message is being transmitted. For now, she is still turning the dial. Watch the video for Return To Dust below: The tension between wonder and uncertainty runs throughout Frankie Rose’s forthcoming album Hila. “Hila is a record about loss,” she says. “What persists beyond the range of ordinary perception? The place mourning keeps returning to — not quite transcendence, not quite doubt. The edge of what we can see.” Self-produced in Rose’s home studio after extensive touring with The Jesus & Mary Chain and Swervedriver, the album also features drummer Justin Welch, known for his work with Elastica and Lush. Its darker passages draw from the esoteric menace of later Coil, the bodily propulsion of Skinny Puppy, and the otherworldly pop vocabulary associated with Cocteau Twins. Yet Return To Dust suggests that Rose’s fascination with these references has become increasingly personal. Genre provides the architecture; bereavement supplies the strange new physics. Listen to Return To Dust below and order the single here. Hila is out September 18 via Born Losers Records worldwide outside the EU and UK, and Night School Records in the EU and UK. Order vinyl here. items.body: Buenos Aires project Sektor Voltage released “En otra dimensión” on June 6, 2026, an eight-track fourth album that mixes electronic body music rhythms with post-punk guitars and coldwave synths. Nicolás Pomilio, who has run the project on his own since 2020, self-released it in digital form. The album is his first to build the songs around guitar rather than around the drum machine. Pomilio describes the shift as a return to what the project was for, not a departure from it: “En otra dimensión (2026) is born: the soul slips beyond the visible, traveling through astral realms. Driven by a motorik pulse, post-punk guitars, futuristic synths, and Nicolás’s cavernous voice, the tracks create dark, danceable atmospheres that hypnotize and transport. Returning to reality is up to the listener.” The eight tracks are “Hojas Negras”, “En otra dimensión”, “In den Verborgenen Wäldern”, “Látigo”, “Cerebro reptil”, “Dornen und Splitter”, “Tu propia sombra” and “Ilusión”. Two carry German titles, and both point at the same reference: the German dark scene of the 1980s, which Pomilio names alongside the old Frankfurt sound and Belgian new beat. He recorded the album on a Zoom R8 portastudio. Drums came from a Kawai R50e and bass from a Korg Monologue, both sequenced over MIDI, with a Yamaha QY10 bass patch used on “Látigo”. Korg Volca FM and Microkorg synths were played live, and percussion, backing vocals and strings were added by hand from a Casio SA keyboard. Guitars and vocals went into Ableton through the Zoom R8’s effects, and the master was finished there too. En otra dimensión by Sektor Voltage The first single, “In den Verborgenen Wäldern”, came with a video directed by Damian Bentrón and Marcelo Moiola and filmed in Rafael Calzada, in the southern Greater Buenos Aires belt, in May 2026. It follows Pomilio alone through open country while the track’s machinery runs underneath. About Sektor Voltage Sektor Voltage is the solo project of Nicolás Pomilio, a producer, guitarist and singer from the southern zone of Greater Buenos Aires, Argentina. He started it in 2020 as an experimental sonic search after working as a DJ and producer in techno, new beat, EBM and darkwave, and turned it into a dark, danceable live set drawn from 1980s sources. Three albums preceded the current one, all self-released and all eight tracks long. “Amor a mi negra lista” arrived on May 14, 2023, followed by “Animal en extinción” on February 11, 2024 and “Oscura noche del alma” on January 28, 2025. Across them Pomilio worked through darkwave, EBM and industrial textures, naming Kraftwerk, Depeche Mode, early Ministry and Front 242 as the starting points. “Oscura noche del alma” also carries a cover of Youth Code‘s “Avengement” and the track “Sexo social” featuring Neuromi. Pomilio has said he felt something was missing after that run, so he made the guitar his main instrument and reworked his voice around the hybrid it produced. The reference points changed with it: post-punk, coldwave and 1980s darkwave, from The Cure and Opéra de Nuit to Malaria!, X-Mal Deutschland and Siekiera. “En otra dimensión” is the first Sektor Voltage record built from that starting point, and it leans on coldwave, goth and post-punk where the earlier releases leaned on EBM and industrial.
items._cn_summary: 阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯单人项目Sektor Voltage的第四张专辑，将原本以鼓机为核心的编曲思路转向吉他主导，融合电子身体音乐节奏、后朋克吉他与冷潮合成器音色。制作上采用Zoom R8便携录音机，配合Kawai R50e鼓机、Korg Monilogue贝斯、Korg Volca FM与Microkorg合成器实时演奏，最后在Ableton中完成混音与母带。专辑主题围绕灵魂穿越星界展开，以motorik脉冲与暗色调人声构建催眠式舞曲氛围。创作动机来源于八十年代德国暗潮场景、法兰克福之声与比利时new beat，展现了对经典暗潮谱系的忠实致敬。

items.body: It’s been a minute since we last heard from jazz guitarist Brad Farberman and his experimental jazz-funk band, Middle Blue, but as you’ll hear on this new Island House Recordings release, it was indeed very much worth the wait. Available today on cassette and digital, Let’s Name a Star on Friday Night is a supremely fun jam record with a bright insatiable energy and heaps of swagger. The album bops with vivacious beats, squealing, honking sax, stanky bass lines and fat wah-wah drenched guitar lines. On tracks like the title cut, soaring melodic clarinets shines side by side with some dirty sax solos, slick drumming and deliciously warped rhythm guitar. As soon as the funky groove of this song catches your ear, it does not let go. This is jazz that is guaranteed for good times. Put this album on when you have company over, and the mood will stay highly elevated til you reach the end…before you inevitably flip the tape over and replay it again and again. If you’re a fan of Joe McPhee, Bobbi Humphrey and Herbie Mann’s work with Sonny Sharrock, then just click here right now to get your copy of this total blast of a record today. -KH
items._cn_summary: Middle Blue Weird Funk 乐队在 Island House Recordings 旗下推出新专辑，以磁带和数字形式发行。吉他手 Brad Farberman 领衔的爵士放克融合作品在节奏律动上充满活力，贝斯线条厚重油腻，吉他大量使用哇音效果，萨克斯尖锐嘶鸣并与高音单簧管形成旋律对话。评论指出标题曲等作品将放克律动与爵士即兴结合，强调此专辑适合派对与社交场合的氛围营造。整体定位偏向娱乐性的放克摇摆气质，尽管包含即兴段落，但评论用词集中在'fun''和'swagge'等轻松愉悦的形容词上，显示出对欢乐情绪的关注高于对前卫探索的兴趣。评论将其与 Joe McPhee、Herbie Mann 等爵士音乐人并列，提示听众这些前辈的实验血脉在新作中的延续。

items.body: “Desilusión” catches the moment an expectation loses its shape and reality takes over. It carries the weight of something that did not go as hoped, and Cisco Pema keeps it that way, without tipping into melodrama. The song moves past that first letdown into acceptance, the turn from expecting something of someone to understanding you needed to stop. It makes that process an intimate song about learning to let go. An Argentine bassist, singer and producer, Pema grew up in Buenos Aires and was on stage from childhood. He moved to Austria for a jazz and improvisation diploma at the Bruckner University, worked as a bassist, composer and producer, then settled in Berlin, where he launched a solo career in 2016. His songs run South American forms through jazz harmony, with traditional and contemporary rhythms underneath. His run of records takes in the self-titled Cisco Pema (2018), Otra realidad (2021) and Tres de Oro (2023), which turns towards rock and pop rock, alongside the 2017 EP Tu Casa Es Mi Casa, made with Munich reggae band Jamaram, that moves between Latin, reggae and dub. Stream “Desilusión” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Cisco Pema – Desilusión appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇介绍阿根廷贝斯手兼制作人Cisco Pema新单曲的文字。作品聚焦于期望落空后的接受与释怀，以内省的方式讲述放手的过程，未陷入过度煽情。音乐上，他以阿根廷音乐为底色，融入爵士和声与传统及当代节奏。此前作品在南美形式与爵士之间架桥，近期开始涉足摇滚与流行摇滚领域，并曾与慕尼黑雷鬼乐队合作，跨越拉丁、雷鬼与Dub风格。这篇文章属于音乐发现类推介，而非深度乐评，信息量适中，提供了艺术家的成长背景与风格谱系，但缺乏对作品具体声音细节与制作层面的分析。

items.body:
On her third studio album, Brooklyn-based artist Frances Chang feels out the boundary between bedroom pop and lavishly orchestrated avant-experimentation, writing on a century-old grand piano and spiking her productions with jerky, unconventional electronic elements. The end result is somewhere between Aimee Mann and Cate Le Bon.

There's something unmistakably ramshackle about Chang's productions, but at the same time, it all sounds as if it's been meticulously planned. On opening track 'I can feel the waves', her voice never falters as it soars over casual phrases from her aging baby grand, but the it's the beats that immediately catch your attention, rupturing the calm with the momentum of a footwork demo. Chang's clearly an obsessive listener and it's this passion that lends her songs a breath of originality; they're classic in a sense, informed by Burt Bacharach, Chet Baker and Dionne Warwick, which actually makes sense. And where she takes the songs after they've been written is fascinating, building them out with instrumentation that's not exactly unexpected, it's just ever so slightly off-kilter. Those warbling strings on the ace 'Bad zen', or the buzzing micro-repetitions on 'Marry' - these sounds just nudge the material into a different zone and assert Chang's personality.

And as it develops, Chang's confidence grows. She's most successful when the guardrails are fully off - like on the brilliant 'No avatar'. Here, she latches her Robert Ashley-esque vocal lead to a wonky synth arpeggio that she follows with piano - or vice versa? The other instruments coolly fall into line: drums, bass and organ seem to flutter, flourish and fall at Chang's command, never quite going in the expected direction. Even advance single 'Auratones of Desire' makes more sense in context, its well-sculpted fusion of psych drum breaks, frittered farfisa organs and soft vocal affectations widening the album's reach considerably. Given it some time and attention for full reward.
items._cn_summary: 这是布鲁克林艺术家张弗兰西斯的第三张录音室专辑。她在一架有近百年历史的大三角钢琴上写作，将卧室流行的私密感与大胆的实验编排并置。制作表面显得松散随意，实则经过精心设计——人声沉稳地漂浮在钢琴的即兴乐句之上，节拍却突然以footwork式的冲击力撕裂平静。歌曲根植于Burt Bacharach、Chet Baker、Dionne Warwick式的经典旋律传统，却在后期制作中引入颤动的弦乐、嗡嗡作响的微重复音色与歪斜的合成器琶音，将素材推向意想不到的方向。她最放得开的时刻出现在《No avatar》，人声线索以Robert Ashley式的口吻展开，鼓、贝斯与风琴随她调度，不走常规路径。整张专辑需要耐心倾听，反复把玩方能体会其中层次。

items.body:
Barnt’s mnml 2012 kosmische waltzer for Matias Aguayo’s Cómeme is repackaged with a new master and Jens-Uwe Beyer + Crato revisions.

The kinky schaeffel is in effect on ‘gaffe’, which takes on a 2nd wind in its brighter, robust remaster, while Jens Uwe-Beyer evens out its irregularities for a disco-ready remix, and best of all, a ‘Magazine Hallucination’ mix that initially jettisons the beat and opens upwards, outward into majestic ambient zones, before its pulled back in a screwed echo of the original waltz groove.
items._cn_summary: Barnt 2012年的minimal techno作品由Cómeme厂牌重新发行，附带全新母带处理与Jens-Uwe Beyer及Crato的混音修订。'gaffe'在新母带中获得了更明亮、更饱满的音色重生，Beyer则抹平了原曲的不规则性，呈现出一个更适合舞池的版本。最突出的是'Magazine Hallucination'混音：先是剥离节拍、向上向外延展至壮丽的环境音域，随后以扭曲回声的方式将原版的三拍圆舞曲律动重新拉回。这种从舞蹈功能到氛围空间的转换，以及对原始素材的结构性解构，体现了Cómeme厂牌一贯的实验性制作美学。整体来看，这是一次对minimal与kosmische传统的探索性重新诠释。

items.body:
Cranky UKG bassbin permutations by a producer with form for Keysound, making his mark on Bristol-via-Berlin’s Sneaker Social Club.

Bare bones rhythms clack and swang in ‘Vintage Gilly’, where aspects of post-dubstep minimalism, electrified halfstep, dark garage and gqom tesselate with a rude UK torque. He recalls Basic Rhythms asceticism on the angular, staccato grime hunch of ‘Drift into Dread’, and the title tune’s rictus, concentrated halfstep, rubbed with Zomby-esque melody, wheres ‘Godkiller’ gives it up for El-B and Sully style darker garage swivel, and ‘Glass Eater’ trades in a sort of warped UKG x gqom mutation.
items._genre: UK garage / bass music / halfstep / gqom mutation
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由一位曾在 Keysound 厂牌发片、现转投 Bristol 与柏林连线厂牌 Sneaker Social Club 的制作人完成，专注于 UKG 低音系统的变体探索。开篇以干涩的碎拍与摇摆节奏为骨架，融入后 dubstep 极简主义、电子化 halfstep、暗黑 garage 与南非 gqom 的切分逻辑，呈现出粗粝的英式力道。'Drift into Dread' 呈现 Basic Rhythm 式的苦行克制，碎裂的 grime 钩子令人侧目；标题曲则是紧绷的 halfstep 构造，辅以 Zomby 式旋律纹理。'Godkiller' 向 El-B 与 Sully 时代更暗的 garage 致敬，'Glass Eater' 则尝试 UKG 与 gqom 的异形杂交。整体手法扎实，融合意图明确，但创新幅度有限，信息量偏少。

items.body:
Ezra Feinberg’s third album Soft Power sees the composer-guitarist enlist an impressive array of fellow musicians including Mary Lattimore, David Moore (Bing & Ruth), Jefre Cantu-Ledesma, and Robbie Lee.

"Defined by its abundance of melodies, repeating figures and ecstatic improvisations, Soft Power exudes an enlightened and transformative spirit to empower the listener. The compassionate, tender-hearted opener ‘Future Sand’ deftly interweaves flutes and steady arpeggios. The Reichian pulse beneath the soaring melody is played not on the customary analogue sequencer, but on finger-picked acoustic guitar, one of the lodestars of Feinberg’s compositional approach. ‘Soft Power’, the buoyant and mesmeric title track that follows builds over a rich bed of guitars and a reverb-y Rhodes melody reminiscent of a Strata East LP, its narrative arc bountiful in energy, optimism and future dreaming, a perfect accompaniment to long days of summertide.

‘Pose Beams’ blends the chamber-jazz approach of Penguin Café Orchestra with a balletic kosmische, climaxing with a galvanising crescendo and “free improv” section performed by fellow New Yorkers - Robbie Lee (piano) and Jefre Cantu-Ledesma, whose granular and modular synths sprinkle particle dust over the expressive drumming of John Thayer. ‘Flutter Intensity’ evokes in part the music of Cluster as played on acoustic guitars, which ping-pong across the stereo field, providing the canvas for a plaintive vibraphone line reminiscent of TNT-era Tortoise. Instruments move in tandem, but also drift and glide allowing them the space to hang in the air, the variegated rhythms, textures, and tones all laced into the fabric of the album.

At the centrefold of the albums 7-tracks is ‘The Big Clock’, a tryptic piece that evolves from pairs of stretched varying tones, creating fields of technicolour over an unabashed motorik beat, serving to offset the pastoral and ambient registers heard elsewhere. It features the first of two appearances from David Moore (Bing & Ruth) who plays lilting piano lines on the come-down. ‘There Was Somebody There’ returns to the album’s earlier wistfulness, a hard stereo-panned soundworld with lightly strummed, interlocking acoustic guitars combining to pigment a washy, painterly scene. David Moore and Jefre Cantu-Ledesma provide reviving synths, the underlying pulse that seems to simulate a life cycle; another day on Earth. The album closes with the reflective ‘Get Some Rest’ featuring Mary Lattimore, whose harp pluckings set a dreamlike tone against bare organic acoustics and flourishing flutes to create a sense of realignment and restoration.

Feinberg artfully transcends the listener to an enriched place, his compositions distinguished by the deep humanity that lies at their core, plugging the listener into a state of wide eyed being, open and alive. Soft Power then is Ezra’s own mantra but also one of power giving - a colourful catharsis translated into music. Feinberg’s music always speaks to the listener, but Soft Power, in whispering, speaks loudest."
items._cn_summary: Ezra Feinberg第三张专辑《Soft Power》邀请Mary Lattimore、David Moore、Jefre Cantu-Ledesma等纽约地下场景音乐人合作，以原声吉他指弹替代模拟序列器构建Reich式脉冲脉律，融合室内爵士、kosmische音乐与新极简主义。开场曲将长笛与稳定琶音交织；标题曲在吉他织体上铺展Rhodes旋律，带有Strata East厂牌的爵士气质。‘Pose Beams’结合Penguin Café Orchestra式室内爵士编排与球形宇宙声响，以即兴段落爆发收束；‘Flutter Intensity’以原声吉他模拟Cluster式声响，在立体声场中构建颗粒质感。‘The Big Clock’以拉伸音色调色板配合强劲motorik节拍。专辑整体在田园氛围与电子律动之间游走，呈现沉思而乐观的精神底色。

items._cn_summary: 大卫·祖宾斯基为普瑞斯姆四重奏创作的《Two Views of a Prayer》是该组合「Unlocking Your Inner Composer」系列协作项目的一部分，2025年11月在费城自由图书馆首演。作品邀请人声艺术家乌苏拉·拉克、打击乐手泰肖恩·索雷以及小提琴家卡洛斯·圣地亚哥共同参与编排与演出，在不到四分钟的篇幅中呈现出从粗粝到抒往返的结构走向。普瑞斯姆四重奏以跨流派、打破常规的演奏风格著称，此曲延续了这一路线，将古典室内乐框架与人声、即兴打击乐、小提琴独奏并置，体现出当代作曲与即兴表演之间的对话尝试。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣界资深歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目大多基于传统音乐素材，融合了口簧琴、风笛、钦巴龙琴、笛子与弦乐等北欧特色乐器，营造出古朴而略带粗粝的氛围。开场曲节奏奔放，充分展示了主唱富有说服力的嗓音；第二首是乐队成员创作的原创作品，器乐层叠推进；末曲则是一首纯器乐作品，口簧琴与笛子、弦乐交织出活泼而略带怪异的听感。作为一支新乐队，作品已展现出超越出道阶段的成熟度，介于北欧传统民谣与世界音乐交叉地带，乐器配置和声乐演绎具有地域文化深度。

items._cn_summary: Finely Tuned Elephant 是来自加拿大的器乐融合四重奏，专辑《No Goats》展现出抓耳的旋律与扎实的技术功底。吉他手 Jordan Robinson 被认为是乐队的核心亮点，演奏风格兼具旋律感与技巧深度。作为器乐融合作品，乐队在爵士、摇滚与前卫元素之间寻找平衡，整体编排紧凑，乐手之间的互动流畅。评论篇幅较短，主要聚焦于第一印象式的描述——抓耳的旋律、过硬的技术与突出的吉他表现——缺乏对具体曲目结构、编曲细节或录音质量的深入分析。对于偏好实验性与前卫融合的听众而言，这张专辑的融合手法偏向传统器乐融合范畴，创新维度有限，但作为融合乐迷的轻松聆听选择仍有一定吸引力。

items.body: German EBM and electro label emmobiz records releases “V.A. 19. Elektrisch Festival” on 24 October 2026, the same day as the 19th Elektrisch Festival at Club Seilerstraße in Zwickau. The 10-inch is pressed on brown vinyl, limited to 222 copies, and sells for 16.99 euro through the label’s own shop. Six tracks from five acts fill the two sides. The record continues an annual series that the label has run since the festival returned in 2024, following the red-vinyl 16th edition and the 17th edition 10-inch, and the 18th, which split across an EBM Edition and a Synth Pop Edition earlier this year. emmobiz describes the Elektrisch series as the only festival compilation of its kind carrying rare or exclusive tracks from the acts on the bill. What is on the 19. Elektrisch Festival 10-inch Four of the five acts on the record play the festival. Portion Control, this year’s headliner, does not appear on the compilation. The label fills the gap with two bonus tracks by acts outside the bill. A1: Escalator, “Utolsókor (Short)”, 3:47 A2: Oszylayter, “we’re the noise”, 4:01 A3: Cyborg Projekt X, “Native Terror” (Vinyl Edit), 3:49 B1: Krieg-B, “kill the light” (V111 Mix), 5:20 B2: Sabotage Q.C.Q.C., “Heidenangst” (Drumatic), 6:05 B3: TöT, “Diers Irae” (Rough Mix), 2:27 The two bonus cuts on the B-side reach outside the festival line-up. Sabotage Q.C.Q.C. are a German electro act who released through Spin Records and EMI Electrola in the 1990s; “Heidenangst” first appeared on their 1996 album “Sexploitation Cinema” and returned in remixed form on the 1997 maxi-single “Schlager”. The version here is a new remake made for this record. Closing the compilation, the Marseille electro-punk and EBM band TöT contribute “Diers Irae”. Escalator, the Budapest EBM band founded in 1988 by 2RT+TB, took their starting point from Kraftwerk and have released since 1989. Oszylayter bring electropunk and breakbeat from Germany. Krieg-B, the Franco-Belgian project Dominique Lallement and Benoît Buyse started in June 2023, follow their emmobiz debut “War Drums’ Resonance” with the album “Concrete Dominion”, which the label also dates to 24 October. About the Elektrisch Festival and emmobiz records The Elektrisch Festival ran five editions in Zwickau between 2007 and 2010, from the 11th to the 15th, at the city’s BPM Club. It then stopped for 14 years. emmobiz records brought it back in 2024 with the 16th edition at Club Seilerstraße, which sold out in advance behind Calva Y Nada, Cat Rapes Dog, Digital Factor and Accessory. The 17th followed in October 2025 and the 18th ran over two evenings in February 2026. The 19th takes place on 24 October 2026 with Portion Control, Escalator, Oszylayter, Cyborg Projekt X and Krieg-B; doors open at 19:00 and the music starts at 20:00. emmobiz records is run by Jörg Freier from Oelsnitz in the Erzgebirge, Saxony, and specialises in industrial, EBM and synthpop. The label stopped operating at the end of 2017 and relaunched on 22 August 2024 with a vinyl reissue of Tyske Ludder’s “Bombt Die Mörder?”. Since then it has reissued the Calva Y Nada catalogue on picture disc, pressed Apoptygma Berzerk’s “Kathy’s Song XXV”, and put out records by Second Decay, Blind Passengers, Fairlight Children and Piston Damp. It organises the festival as well as documenting it, and the 10-inch goes on sale the day the doors open.
items._cn_summary: 本文为德国EBM与电子厂牌emmobiz records发行的第19届Elektrisch Festival十寸黑胶合集介绍，限量222张棕色乙烯基，收录五位艺人的六首曲目。内容以信息性新闻稿为主，包含曲目列表、艺人简介和厂牌背景。A面三位艺人Escalator、Oszylayter、Cyborg Projekt X均参与本届音乐节演出，B面除Krieg-B外另收录两条非演出阵容的特别曲目，包括Sabotage Q.C.Q.C. 1996年老曲的新混音版及马赛电子朋克乐队TöT的作品。作为厂牌的年度节庆合集延续项目，定位偏传统EBM和electro范畴，曲目以remix和混音版本为主，实验性和创新性有限，更接近节庆纪念性质的合辑而非艺术性制作。
