items.body: Chicago industrial and darkwave artist I Ya Toyah released “Closer”, a cover of the Nine Inch Nails song, on 21 August 2026 through her own label Femme Fatale Records. It is a digital single, and it arrives with a video the same week. On Bandcamp the artist describes the release in a single line: “This is the cover of Nine Inch Nail’s song.” Closer by I Ya Toyah The original was written by Michael Trent Reznor and appeared on Nine Inch Nails‘ 1994 album “The Downward Spiral”. I Ya Toyah produced this version with Johnny K, who also mixed it. Howie Weinberg mastered the track and Angelica Dulany supplied the artwork. Publishing runs through Leaving Hope Music and TVT Music, with the cover licensed through Easy Song Licensing. “Closer” is the third single I Ya Toyah has issued through Femme Fatale Records this year, after the two-track “Feelings” on 1 May and “Apology” on 26 June. Johnny K mixed and produced all three, and Howie Weinberg mastered them. Her press release describes the run as a completed trilogy about the forces that shape identity. The ‘Closer’ video The video was filmed and directed by Alex Zarek, who edited it with I Ya Toyah. The concept is hers. Angelica Dulany handled production assistance and additional direction, Janet Debris did makeup and Allison Ciletti managed the location. It went up on her own YouTube channel on 21 August 2026. The single is on Bandcamp and on the usual streaming services through a single smart link. About I Ya Toyah I Ya Toyah is the solo project of Ania Tarnowska, a Polish-born musician, producer and engineer based in the Chicago area. The name comes from Polish, where the spoken phrase reads as “it’s just me”. She trained on classical guitar, piano and voice as a child, studied music business and audio engineering at the SAE Institute in 2016, and started the project in 2017 with the single “Funeral For Love”. The debut album “Code Blue” followed on 26 October 2018, self-released, with the single “Farewell – Mirrors Don’t Lie” alongside it. The catalogue after that ran quickly. “Code Blue Reloaded” and “Code Blue Revelations” both landed in 2020, the five-part EP “Out of Order” in 2021 and the acoustic EP “Ghosts” in 2022. “Panic Room” arrived in 2023, produced with Walter Flakus of Stabbing Westward, whose US dates she opened that year. Flakus also worked on the “I am the Fire” EP and the album “DRAMA”, both 2024, the year Side-Line covered her video for ‘Fraud’ and talked to her about the new album. She has been a member of The Joy Thieves since 2019 and toured with Pigface the same year. Remixers and collaborators across the catalogue include Rhys Fulber, who remixed “Flashback” in 2019, Tim Skold, who remixed “Motion” in 2020, and Julian Beeston of Nitzer Ebb, whose “We The People”, “Higher Than The Sun” and “Crazy Horses” all feature her. She has also remixed PIG’s “The New Disorder”. In 2024 she toured the United States with Orgy and Cold and played her first European dates supporting Front Line Assembly, and she returned to Europe in February and March 2026 as direct support on KMFDM’s tour. Femme Fatale Records, her own imprint, has carried her releases since 2024 and now issues “Closer”.
items._cn_summary: 芝加哥工业暗潮艺术家I Ya Toyah发布了Nine Inch Nails经典曲目《Closer》的翻唱版本，作为其个人厂牌Femme Fatale Records今年推出的第三支单曲，构成关于身份塑造力量的三部曲终章。制作由Johnny K操刀混音与编曲，Howie Weinberg负责母带处理，整体保留了原作的工业暗潮骨架。音乐人Ania Tarnowska拥有古典吉他、钢琴与声乐训练背景，作品目录涵盖暗潮、工业、电子等多种风格，与Stabbing Westward成员Walter Flakus以及Rhys Fulber、Tim Skold等工业电子领域知名制作人有过合作。她还是The Joy Thieves成员，并曾为Pigface巡演。配套MV由Alex Zarek执导拍摄。整体来看，这是一篇发布信息详实但缺乏深度乐评的资讯类文章，未对翻唱版本的音乐特色、制作细节或艺术处理进行分析与评价。

items.body: Made in secret in the shadow of Soviet Normalization, after decades as a cult object Maťkovia's debut album has been newly reissued and expanded. Jakub Knera tells the extraordinary story of the project's leader Martin Burlas ‘Normalization’ in Czechoslovakia in the 1970s and 1980s was paradoxical: rather than a return to normality, it in fact meant renewed state control over society, culture, and public life. It followed the Prague Spring of 1968, which had grown out of the political and cultural relaxation of the 1960s, where under Alexander Dubček, reforms aimed to create ‘socialism with a human face’ allowed greater freedom of expression and artistic experimentation. The Soviet Union considered these reforms too radical, however, and in August 1968 Warsaw Pact... The post Reissue of the Week: Maťkovia’s 1982 – 1986 (Expanded) appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 本文聚焦斯洛伐克乐手Martin Burlas领导的Maťkovia项目，其1982年首作在铁幕后秘密录制，现以扩展版本重新发行。乐评追溯了1968年布拉格之春后的捷克“正常化”时期国家如何收紧对文化生活的管控，这张专辑正是被压抑状态下诞生的地下产物。重新发行版本加入了1986年的后续作品，呈现了在政治高压下仍坚持进行的实验性音乐探索。专辑以沉寂多年的cult收藏品身份重现，为理解东欧地下音乐史与冷战时期先锋声音实验提供了罕见的窗口。本文为新闻性质发行报道，对音乐本身的音色、创作技法及听感分析着墨甚少，信息量偏向历史背景而非音乐本体。

items.album: VOLKER KRIEGEL Keep on Driving (with Don "Sugar Cane" Harris) (Jazz Rock/Fusion, 1970)
items.excerpt: Review by BrufordFreak — With everybody on board employing electric or amplified sound what we have here is some true Jazz-Rock Fusion (of the Herbie Hancock Mwandishi school of influence). The album's material (of all original Don Harris compositions) was recorded on November 17 and 18, 1970, at MPS Tonstudio in Villingen, Germany, and then released soon thereafter (probably in early 1971).WARNING: This is really a Don "Sugar Cane" Harris album: Volker Kriegel is just a collaborating gues
items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — With everybody on board employing electric or amplified sound what we have here is some true Jazz-Rock Fusion (of the Herbie Hancock Mwandishi school of influence). The album's material (of all original Don Harris compositions) was recorded on November 17 and 18, 1970, at MPS Tonstudio in Villingen, Germany, and then released soon thereafter (probably in early 1971).WARNING: This is really a Don "Sugar Cane" Harris album: Volker Kriegel is just a collaborating guest; all song compositions are credited solely to Don Harris.1. "Keep On Driving" (4:05) music solidly rooted in Blues and Blues-Rock traditions on which Volker and Sugar Cane take turns presenting the "Proud Mary"-like main melody and their variations and improvisational interpretations thereof. Already one can sense how dextrously-talented Volker is. John Taylor must be playing an early version of an electric piano as it sounds quite odd (and primitive). The rhythmatists are playing something quite basic and simplistic, following the main melody line quite closely, which feels rather amateurish. (8.75/10)2. "Blues On The Moon" (6:53) unstructured bass play with virtually solo violin improvising some melody over the top while John, Volker, and Tony Oxley play with experimental sound-making from behind the scenes. Toward the fourth minute the bass, drums, and electric piano start to gel into some kind of loose three-chord vamp as Sugar Cane continues exploring his own bluesy melody line. The song begins to deconstruct and bottom out slowly almost from the five-minute mark on with no one else really getting much solo time, everybody just kind of loosely jamming to that three-chord vamp. (13.125/15)3. "Which Way Is The Bathroom?" (4:02) electric violin begins soloing Jean-Luc Ponty-like from the opening note over two-chord electric piano, bass, and touch-drive drums, switching the rhythm track a bit in the second minute as Sugar Cane peaks. Volker enters in the second half of the second minute, truly ripping a few jaw-dropping slurring shred-lines before giving up the spotlight first to John Taylor, then Tony Oxley, before Sugar Cane returns in the fourth minute to take back the lead, rhythm section slowing down and spacing things out a bit as Sugar Cane really flies. Then the song is slowly faded out. (8.875/10)4. "Desiree" (8:40) a slower paced, cool spacious jazz motif that sounds inspired by the old Miles Kind of Blue album while the piano has gone electric, the bass, too, and the melodic violin is also electrified. I really like the way Tony Oxley's drums are recorded: nice full toms and crisp, clear cymbals. The only other soloist on the song is John Taylor on his electric piano; Volker is absent from this one. A nice, laid-back tune that offers nice solos but nothing jaw-dropping or ground-breaking. (17.667/20)5. "Almost Broke" (5:58) electric piano play from John Taylor sounds like a Vibraphone, the amazing bass play is Sugar Cane! Which means multiple tracks were used in recording this one. Volker gets some nice solo time but really has little contributions otherwise: it's mostly Don, John, and drummer Tom Oxley performing as the rhythm trio with Volker and Sugar Cane taking some turns with electric guitar and electric violin, respectively. (9/10)6. "Coitus Interruptus" (4:58) Mississippi Swamp Blues with Volker playing rhythm with Sugar Cane's bass while Cane's wah-wah-treated electric violin presents the bluesy main melody from the opening note (sounding a bit like a dobro!) Cool sound! Volker takes over the lead around 1:50 with some raunchy distortion and overdrive adding a stinky stank to his solo (and the music). John Taylor is next, his also-stinky distorted electric piano is mixed in an odd left-back position (opposite Volker). A little flashiness from Tony precedes Sugar Cane's re-entry with his squawky violin. Kind of a cool sound despite its very rudimentary blues construction. (8.875/10)7. "Remember The Past" (10:08) again John Taylor's jazzy Herbie Hancock-like electric piano play coupled with Don's slow-struttin' bass and Tony's excellent spacious drum play give Sugar Cane the chance to really spill his guts with his treated electric and acoustic violins. Volker doesn't really make his presence known until the fourth minute: once Cane has finished his first extended solo. Volker's solo is pretty standard jazz guitar until he starts shred-bending his guitar strings as if he were Sonny Sharrock, Chris Spedding, Pete Townsend, or Roye Albrighton. Then John gets a turn, occupying the seventh minute before some guitar scratching signals time for a bass solo (during which Volker continues to play with the feedback effects on his electric guitar). The band comes back to the opening theme for the final minute as Sugar Cane closes things up with his plaintive melody (while Volker and/or Tony continue to play with electronically-induced sound effects). Kind of cool experimental stuff within some laid-back down-home front porch smooth jazz. (17.75/20)Total Time 44:44I am definitely surprised by how little Volker Kriegel's contributions are considered: he's mostly there to provide solos only--often very brief ones at that. In contrast, I'm also surprised by the how much creative input drummer Tony Oxley and electric pianist John Taylor are given. And, lastly, who knew that Don Harris was such a bass player (and composer)?! B/four stars; a solid contribution of early experimental Jazz-Rock Fusion.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张1970年录制于德国Villingen的爵士摇滚融合专辑，实质上是小提琴手Don "Sugar Cane" Harris主导的作品，吉他手Volker Kriegel仅为合作嘉宾。所有曲目均为Harris原创，融合了蓝调、爵士摇滚与自由即兴元素。专辑中电小提琴与电钢琴展开Jean-Luc Ponty式的对话，Tony Oxley的鼓声录制饱满清晰，镲片清脆。某些段落以松散的三和弦vamp为基础进行集体即兴探索，低音提琴与电小提琴在简约节奏上自由漂浮。整体风格受Herbie Hancock Mwandishi系列影响，但部分曲目结构较为松散，节奏组表现被评价为基础且业余。专辑在即兴自由度和实验性音色探索上有一定价值，但创新性和突破性有限，属于较为常规的早期爵士摇滚跨界尝试。

items.body: Dutch new wave duo Pol released the official video for “Sex Machines” on 21 August 2026. Fashion photographer and filmmaker Rémi Lamandé directed it. The single itself came out on 25 June 2026 as a two-track digital release on Bandcamp, pairing the 3:59 vocal version with an instrumental of the same length, and is also on streaming platforms. Pol are the brothers Ruben and Matthijs Pol, who are based in Paris. They gave “Sex Machines” a single launch show during Paris Fashion Week in June 2026, two months before the video appeared. How Pol built the ‘Sex Machines’ video Lamandé built the clip as a street interview programme. Ruben Pol carries a star-marked microphone through a service alley and holds it out to a series of passers-by, each of whom lip-syncs the lyric instead of answering. The cast then moves into a concrete parking garage, and the closing section shows the duo performing to a packed room under hard white backlight. A final outtake shows the two brothers laughing. The duo explained where the concept started: “It started off with the idea of doing an interview style video with a diverse cast of characters. We liked the idea of ‘strangers’ singing the song, similarly how the two ex-lovers in the lyrics are acting like strangers. We shared the idea with director Remi Lamandé who brought the full script to life.” The brothers wrote and produced the track themselves. Matthijs Pol plays drum computer, electric guitar, synths, xylophone and sings; Ruben Pol plays drum computer, electric guitar, synths, bass, vocoder and sings. Matthijs and Ruben mixed it with Paul D. Millar, and Gianni Peri mastered it. On their own Bandcamp page the duo describe the song as built on “twitching beats, serrated guitars and clipped vocals”. Sex Machines by Pol About Pol Pol is a duo formed by the Dutch brothers Ruben and Matthijs Pol, now based in Paris, France. Both play guitar, synthesizers and drum computer and both sing; Ruben adds bass and vocoder, Matthijs adds xylophone. The pair write, produce and mix their own recordings and handle their visuals, videos, merchandise and fanzines themselves. The brothers issued a self-titled debut EP in 2023. Two singles followed on their own Bandcamp: “Masks” in June 2024 and “The Chameleon” in December 2024. Their first zine, which documents a Western European tour, is stocked by the Paris bookshop Librairie 1909, and the same multidisciplinary practice has produced sound-design work for Louis Vuitton and Miu Miu. In 2024 the duo played their first headline show at a sold-out Bitterzoet in Amsterdam with Logan Sky of Visage, and have since performed in Europe, the United States and Japan. In early 2026 they opened sold-out Lebanon Hanover shows in London, Lille and Paris. “Sex Machines”, released on 25 June 2026, is their first new music since “The Chameleon”. The Rémi Lamandé video, out on 21 August 2026, is the first visual the duo have released from it.
items._cn_summary: Pol是一支由荷兰兄弟Ruben和Matthijs组成的二人组合，现居巴黎。他们于2026年6月发行单曲《Sex Machines》，并于8月发布由时尚摄影师兼电影制作人Rémi Lamandé执导的官方MV。歌曲以鼓机、电吉他、合成器、木琴和人声为基础，官方描述为"抽搐的节拍、锯齿状的吉他与断裂的人声"。MV采用街头采访形式，由Ruben手持星形麦克风走访路人，陌生人对口型演唱歌词而非真正回答，暗合歌词中两位前恋人形同陌路的概念。二人自写自产自混，还曾为Louis Vuitton和Miu Miu做声音设计，视觉、周边与自制zine均由自己操持。此前曾为Lebanon Hanover暖场，展现出与暗潮圈层的关联。整体呈现DIY美学与暗黑新浪潮气质的结合。原文为新闻通稿，缺乏深度评论。

items.body: Leipzig darkwave project Kalte Steine released “Drowning” on 20 August 2026 as a self-released digital single. The track runs 4:39 and is available on Bandcamp and on streaming services. It is the project’s sixth single and the second sung entirely in English, following “Crying Out” from June 2026. Kalte Steine mix darkwave and post-punk: drum machine, bass, a spare guitar figure and vocals set well back in delay and reverb. On “Drowning” a field recording of waves opens the track before the rhythm section enters, and buzzing analogue synthesizers arrive about a minute in. Drowning by Kalte Steine Where ‘Drowning’ sits in the Kalte Steine catalogue The project’s first four singles, “Shattered”, “Dysthymia”, “Wüste aus Beton” and “Kinder der Nacht”, were sung in German and appeared on Bandcamp in June 2026. “Crying Out”, issued on 29 June 2026, was the first Kalte Steine track written and sung in English. “Drowning” continues in that language. All six tracks are self-released. Kalte Steine has no label, no album and no Discogs entry, and sells its catalogue directly through Bandcamp at a per-track price. The digital track download is offered in MP3, FLAC and 24-bit/44.1 kHz formats. About Kalte Steine Kalte Steine is a darkwave and post-punk project based in Leipzig, Germany. The project releases under its own name without a label and has not published a lineup, so the number of people involved is not documented. Recording activity began in mid-2026. Four German-language singles, “Shattered”, “Dysthymia”, “Wüste aus Beton” and “Kinder der Nacht”, went up on Bandcamp in June 2026, tagged by the project as alternative, darkwave, goth, gothic and post-punk. Those tracks set out the recording approach the project has kept since: drum machine, bass, single-line guitar, synthesizer, and vocals treated with delay and reverb rather than pushed forward in the mix. “Crying Out” arrived on 29 June 2026 and switched the writing to English. “Drowning” followed on 20 August 2026 as the second English-language track and the sixth release overall. Both are available on Bandcamp and on streaming platforms, and no physical edition has been issued.
items._cn_summary: 来自德国莱比锡的暗潮项目Kalte Steine于2026年8月20日发行单曲《Drowning》，这是其第六首单曲及第二首全英文作品。曲风融合暗潮与后朋克，编制以鼓机、贝斯、单线吉他及模拟合成器为主，人声被推至混音深处并施加延迟与混响处理，营造出距离感。歌曲开头使用海浪实地录音，随后节奏部分进入，约一分钟时嗡嗡作响的模拟合成器铺陈开来。整首作品延续了项目自首批德语单曲以来确立的声响路径，未签约厂牌，自行通过Bandcamp以单曲形式发行数字版本，提供MP3、FLAC及24-bit/44.1kHz格式下载。该项目没有正式阵容披露，所有成员身份均未公开。

items.body: Todd Stephens’s 2001 goth road movie is back in United States cinemas as Gypsy 83: The Director’s Cut, restored in 4K from the original 35mm camera negative and re-edited to 138 minutes, against the 95 minutes of the version released in 2001. The new edition adds over 40 minutes of previously unseen footage and further goth soundtrack cues, including songs by The Cure, Cocteau Twins and Echo & The Bunnymen. Altered Innocence is handling the theatrical release, which opened at New York’s Quad Cinema on 14 August 2026 and continues across the country into September. The restoration was assembled for the film’s 25th anniversary. Stephens recut the picture with editor Anderson Matthew, and the 35mm elements recovered for the project became the basis of the 4K scan. What the ‘Gypsy 83’ director’s cut changes The story is unchanged. Gypsy Vale, played by Sara Rue, and her younger friend Clive Webb, played by Birkett Turton, are goth outsiders and Stevie Nicks fans in Sandusky, Ohio. When they hear that a New York club is staging a Night of 1000 Stevies, the two drive east so that Gypsy can perform. Karen Black plays lounge singer Bambi LeBleau, and John Doe of the punk band X plays Gypsy’s father, Ray. Paulo Costanzo and Anson Scoville complete the principal cast. What changes is length and music. At 138 minutes the director’s cut carries more than 40 minutes of material cut from the 2001 release, and the extra running time makes room for additional soundtrack placements. Alongside The Cure, Cocteau Twins and Echo & The Bunnymen, the expanded music bed draws on Ministry, Clan Of Xymox, Alien Sex Fiend and Switchblade Symphony, plus Diva Destruction’s cover of “Talk to Me” and Nobody’s Wolf Child’s reading of “Song to the Siren”. Gypsy 83 was Stephens’s directorial debut. He had written and produced the 1998 film “Edge of Seventeen”, and returned to Sandusky, his home town, for “Swan Song” in 2021; the three films are grouped as his Ohio trilogy. The trailer for the director’s cut is below. ‘Gypsy 83’ theatrical dates 14 to 20 August 2026 – New York, NY – Quad Cinema 21 to 27 August 2026 – Los Angeles, CA – Nuart Theatre (Q&A with Todd Stephens, Birkett Turton and cinematographer Gina DeGirolamo on 21 and 22 August at 7 p.m.) 26 and 27 August 2026 – Seattle, WA – SIFF Film Center 27 August 2026 – San Francisco, CA – The Roxie Theater 29 August 2026 – Houston, TX – River Oaks Theatre 31 August 2026 – Nashville, TN – Belcourt Theatre 3 September 2026 – Philadelphia, PA – PhilaMOCA 4 to 10 September 2026 – Howell, MI – Historic Howell Theater 10 September 2026 – Sacramento, CA – The Dreamland Cinema 11 to 17 September 2026 – Denver, CO – Sie FilmCenter Blu-ray and DVD pre-orders are open through Altered Innocence, with the home video release set for later this year. About Gypsy 83 Gypsy 83 was written and directed by Todd Stephens and produced in 2001, following his screenplay for “Edge of Seventeen” three years earlier. Shot on 35mm and set in Sandusky, Ohio, the film follows two goth outsiders driving to New York City for the Night of 1000 Stevies, an annual Stevie Nicks tribute event. Sara Rue plays Gypsy Vale, Birkett Turton plays Clive Webb, Karen Black plays Bambi LeBleau, and John Doe of X plays Gypsy’s father. Gina DeGirolamo shot the film. The original 95-minute cut ran in cinemas in 2001 and later reached home video and streaming services. Its soundtrack placed goth and post-punk records at the centre of the two leads’ sense of themselves, and a 2003 soundtrack compilation collected part of that music. Stephens returned to Sandusky twice more. “Edge of Seventeen” (1998) and “Swan Song” (2021) sit either side of Gypsy 83 in what he groups as an Ohio trilogy about queer lives in a Midwestern city. For the 25th anniversary, Stephens and editor Anderson Matthew rebuilt the film from the recovered 35mm camera negative. The result, running 138 minutes, is the version now in United States cinemas through Altered Innocence, with a home video release to follow later in 2026.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非乐评，而是关于2001年哥特公路电影《Gypsy 83》导演剪辑版重映的新闻报道。影片由Altered Innocence负责院线发行，以4K分辨率从原始35mm底片修复，片长从95分钟扩展至138分钟，新增超过40分钟未公开素材。核心变化在于原声带的扩充，纳入了The Cure、Cocteau Twins、Echo & The Bunnymen等经典乐队曲目，同时加入Ministry、Clan Of Xymox、Alien Sex Fiend、Switchblade Symphony等更偏向暗潮与工业方向的作品，另收录Diva Destruction翻唱及Nobody's Wolf Child改编曲目。文章附带完整的北美巡映日程，从纽约Quad Cinema启程，途经洛杉矶、西雅图、旧金山等多座城市的艺术影院。内容聚焦电影修复事件本身而非音乐分析，但所提及的配乐阵容对暗潮与后朋克听众具有参考价值。

items.body: Sentient Ruin Laboratories will issue Marca Diaboli’s debut EP “Labyrintomb” on vinyl on September 11, 2026, the first time the five-track record has been pressed. The Oakland label describes the project as a Chilean-Austrian occult rock, post-punk and black metal act, and the EP first appeared on October 31, 2025 as a cassette limited to sixty copies on the German label Sect Entropy. The vinyl is a single-sided 12″ with the B-side silkscreened in metallic gold ink, housed in a matte sleeve printed black inside, with an insert inlay and a download card. Two pressings exist: a crystal clear edition of one hundred copies worldwide, sold direct by the label and not distributed to shops, and a standard black edition. Three of the five test pressings are also being offered, hand-numbered, signed, and packaged in a black fold-over cover silkscreened in gold. “Labyrintomb” runs eighteen minutes across “Digging Graves”, “Nightfalls”, “Arsonists”, “Manifest” and “The Last Nail”. It was recorded and performed by a single musician credited as M.R.C. between May and June 2025 in Lower Austria, with Krsfrs mixing and M.R.C. mastering. Steven Henningsard cut the vinyl master and Svart Graphics handled the cover art and layout. Sentient Ruin calls the EP “a grave-born spell book of primeval shamanic rock musick” and names In Solitude, Negative Plane, Bauhaus, Amebix and The Devil’s Blood as its reference points. The lo-fi production comes out of black metal, but the melodies and the pacing sit closer to post-punk and early-1990s underground rock than to anything in that genre. Labyrintomb by MARCA DIABOLI About Marca Diaboli Marca Diaboli was conceived in the forests of Lower Austria and dates its own founding to 2025. The label’s account puts the project’s first public step in the summer of that year, when the track “Nightfalls” was self-released digitally on Bandcamp, and its debut proper at the end of October 2025 with the “Labyrintomb” cassette on Sect Entropy. The project works as a one-person operation on record: M.R.C. performs everything and shares the credits only with a mixing engineer and the vinyl and artwork staff. No member names have been published beyond those initials, and the Chilean side of the Chilean-Austrian description has not been detailed by the band or the label. Its stated sources are late-1980s and early-1990s underground rock, post-punk and metal, the rawest end of second-wave black metal, and contemporary dark rock. Beyond “Labyrintomb” and the “Nightfalls” single, the project has released nothing else. The September vinyl is its first release for Sentient Ruin, a label that has spent a decade working the edges of black metal, doom, noise and post-punk out of Oakland, California.
items._genre: occult rock / post-punk / black metal / lo-fi
items._cn_summary: 这则乐评实为唱片发行新闻，介绍智利-奥地利一人乐队首张EP的黑胶再版信息。原磁带于2025年万圣节在德国厂牌限量发行六十盒，现由奥克兰独立厂牌Sentient Ruin Laboratories首次压制成单面12寸黑胶，B面以金属金色丝网印刷，附哑光封套与下载卡。十八分钟内容跨越五首曲目，由单人M.R.C.在奥地利下奥地利州录制完成，制作粗糙，旋律与节奏更贴近后朋克与九十年代初地下摇滚，而非典型黑金属。评论提到参考对象如In Solitude、Negative Plane、Bauhaus、Amebix与The Devil's Blood。厂牌将其描述为'诞生于坟墓的原始萨满摇滚咒语之书'，但实际文字并未深入探讨音乐本身的创新性或艺术价值，整体偏重发行格式与厂牌背景的信息性报道。

The page opened on June 12, 2026 and filled up one song at a time, closing with “Blu-Green Beauty” on August 13, 2026. The running order is “In Other Words” (3:44), “Thirty Pieces” (3:50), “I Ain’t Goin!” (2:21) and “Blu-Green Beauty” (4:56). Bullock wrote, produced, performed and
items.body: New Jersey dark rock and post-punk musician Greg Bullock has finished “26EP”, a self-released four-track EP he built in public on Bandcamp. The page opened on June 12, 2026 and filled up one song at a time, closing with “Blu-Green Beauty” on August 13, 2026. The running order is “In Other Words” (3:44), “Thirty Pieces” (3:50), “I Ain’t Goin!” (2:21) and “Blu-Green Beauty” (4:56). Bullock wrote, produced, performed and mixed everything himself, playing vocals, hardware and software synthesizers and arranging the drum tracks. He recorded at his own GABWorx, Studio B; Mark Trewella mastered at Full Circle Mastering. The cover and track photos are Bullock’s own. The closing track is the plainest of the four in intent. Bullock sums it up in a single line on its Bandcamp page: “Our world is not the dump that humans treat it as.” The lead track, “In Other Words”, turns on ignorance, persecution and contaminated morality, subjects Bullock has called “ideas we may not want to think about.” The EP is digital and carries no label. Bullock spreads it across goth rock, post-punk, synth rock and a strain of alt-country, so no two of the four tracks sit in quite the same place. Greg Bullock – 26EP by Greg Bullock About Greg Bullock Greg Bullock is a musician and producer based in Plumsted Township, New Jersey, where he runs the GABWorx studio. He is best known as co-founder, vocalist and keyboard player of Cyborg Amok, the duo he started in 2019 with his son Brydon Bullock on drums and vocals. The pair describe that project as gothic-infused synth-rock; their most recent album, “Pins & Needles”, came out in April 2025. Bullock’s solo catalogue runs alongside it and shares the same Bandcamp page, which also carries Brydon’s own tracks. He gathered his earlier work on “Best Of … so far!” in September 2025, then released the standalone single “No Exit” the following month. A second Bandcamp account under the GABWorx name holds the albums “Etiam” and “The Language Angels Speak In The Darkness”. “26EP” is his first multi-track solo release since that 2025 collection, and the first he assembled in the open rather than shipping complete. There is no video for any of the four tracks; the EP is available on Bandcamp and on the streaming services.
items._genre: dark rock / post-punk / synth rock / alt-country
items._cn_summary: Greg Bullock独立完成了这张四曲EP的全部创作、演奏、制作与混音工作，在自己的GABWorx工作室中完成录制。四首曲目分别聚焦不同的社会议题，如闭幕曲以一句关于环境保护的宣言概括其核心立场，首曲则触及无知、迫害与道德污染等沉重主题。整张EP在哥特摇滚、后朋克、合成器摇滚与另类乡村之间游走，没有两首曲子处于完全相同的风格位置。作为他首次以公开逐步发布形式构建的多曲作品，这种制作方式本身具有实验性与透明度。封面与曲目摄影亦由本人完成，整体呈现出高度自主的DIY美学。

items.body: Neapolitan project Fiori del Male released “Allarme rosso nel golfo persico” on April 4, 2026, thirty-five years after Nunzio Ciccone wrote it. The five-minute track sets an anti-war lyric against post-punk guitars, alternative rock instrumentation and electronics, and had sat unreleased since 1991. Ciccone wrote it in Scampia, in the northern outskirts of Naples, while the first Gulf War was being broadcast live. The lyric is about that broadcast rather than the fighting: propaganda, saturation coverage, and what happens when a war arrives in a living room through a television set. Ciccone sings and Andrea Palazzo plays guitar, with Vincenzo Esposito on bass and Claudio Ciccone handling DJ work and production. The New York engineer known as MisterAC mastered it. The single is self-released under the Nunzio Ciccone Bros. imprint and distributed digitally; it is on Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer and YouTube, and there is no physical edition and no music video. About Fiori del Male Fiori del Male formed in Scampia, Naples in the early 1990s around Nunzio Ciccone, who has led it under several names since. The group first worked as Flowers Of Evil, the English rendering of the same phrase, then as FlowerPeace after moving to Milan in 1998. In 2000 the members relocated to London and stayed there until 2012, writing and recording in the city for twelve years before returning to Naples in 2014. The project is now spread between Rome, London and Naples, and works as a collective rather than a fixed lineup: Ciccone, his siblings Claudio and Alessia Ciccone, and a rotating set of players including Palazzo and Esposito. Recorded output has been sparse. The single “E’ solo un giorno che non va, con la luna dentro gli occhi” appeared on April 30, 2020, credited to Ciccone with Alessia Ciccone, Vincenzo Esposito, Armando Vertullo, Danilo Napoli, Roberto Zincone and Fiori del Male. “Angeli Ribelli” followed on July 31, 2023. “Allarme rosso nel golfo persico” is the third release under the name in six years, and the oldest piece of writing among them by a wide margin. Note for readers searching for the project: a separate Italian black metal duo from Brindisi also records as Fiori del Male, and several streaming services merge the two into one artist page. They are unrelated.
items._cn_summary: 那不勒斯项目Fiori del Male于2026年发行单曲《Allarme rosso nel golfo persico》，这首作品实际由Nunzio Ciccone于1991年海湾战争期间在那不勒斯郊区Scampia创作，却尘封三十五年才面世。五分钟的曲目将反战歌词置于后朋克吉他、独立摇滚器乐与电子声响的交汇处，主题聚焦于战争如何通过电视直播侵入日常生活：宣传话语、饱和报道与媒介化的暴力。Ciccone主唱，Andrea Palazzo演奏吉他，Vincenzo Esposito担任贝斯，Claudio Ciccone负责DJ与制作，纽约工程师MisterAC完成母带处理。作品以自我厂牌独立发行，仅作数字分发，无实体版本。乐队经历从Scampia到米兰再到伦敦的多次迁移，成员以集体形式运作，发行极为稀疏，三十六年间仅积累三首作品，此曲为其中最古老的一首。

items.body: Aggrotech and dark electro project Subliminal Code released “Behind the Mask” through Neon Retro Records on July 31, 2026, and expanded it on August 16 with a fifth track. The label edition carried four cuts; the version on the project’s own Bandcamp page adds a remix by Dominator. The full running order is the title track (4:35), a People Theatre remix (5:01), an Elektroterapi remix (2:48), a club version (4:35) and the Dominator remix (3:15). Raúl J. Padrón wrote, produced and sang it and drew the artwork; Raúl Jr. Padrón handled synths and programming; Vitor Mancini mixed and mastered. The source material is horror cinema, and the project says so plainly on the release page: “Inspired by the dark atmosphere of classic slasher horror films, Behind the Mask tells the story of an unstoppable killer lurking in the shadows, where every step could be your last. Cold synths, crushing beats, distorted vocals, and relentless aggression come together to create the soundtrack for your darkest nightmare.” Three of the four extra versions push the track further toward the dancefloor than the original does, moving it from aggrotech and dark electro toward industrial techno. The release is digital. Behind the Mask by Subliminal Code About Subliminal Code Subliminal Code was founded at the start of 2010 by Raúl José Padrón and Raúl Junior Padrón, drawing on EBM, industrial, metal and synthpop. The project began in Venezuela and is now based in Budapest, Hungary, where Raúl José Padrón carries it as the sole permanent member. The first release, the “Soldier Of Hell” EP, appeared on December 23, 2011 through Engraved Ritual, followed by the single “The Beautiful People” in 2013 and “Another Day” on March 24, 2014. The debut album “Karma In Mortem” arrived on July 14, 2014 on the Hungarian label Advoxya Records, which then issued “Karma In Covers” on November 1, 2016 – a set of covers of Venezuelan metal bands – and “Soldier Of Hell, Reborn” three days later. In 2016 the project also appeared on Insane Records’ compilation “Terror Night Vol.2 Sound Of Dead Future”. Side-Line covered the single “Malevolencia” when it appeared on February 29, 2020, trailing the second album. That album, “The Cancer Of The World Is Human Beings”, came out on May 1, 2021 on Advoxya with eleven tracks. Since then the project has worked mainly in singles and short releases: the seven-track “I Never” on September 1, 2022, “Push Me Down” that November, “Memento Mori” on October 10, 2023, “Your Wish” on July 20, 2024 and “Void Of Morgoth” on July 15, 2025. “Behind the Mask” is the first Subliminal Code release to carry Neon Retro Records, a synthwave netlabel running since July 2019, and the first to be built out as a remix package rather than a standalone track.

items._cn_summary: Subliminal Code 由委内瑞拉出身、现居布达佩斯的 Padrón 父子创立，最新单曲「Behind the Mask」以经典砍杀恐怖片为灵感，通过 Neon Retro Records 发行数字版本，并随后在 Bandcamp 追加第五首 Dominator 混音。整张作品由 Raúl J. Padrón 创作并演唱，他本人亦负责封面设计，Raúl Jr. Padrón 负责合成器与编程，Vitor Mancini 完成混音与母带。标题曲及三个混音版本将原始的暗潮工业质感进一步推向工业 techno 方向，强化了俱乐部语境下的冲击力。五首曲目以不同的节奏与音色处理呈现同一素材的多种面貌，编曲重心明确放在冷峻合成器音色、失真人声与高密度节拍的堆叠上。

items.body: Melanculia is a project driven by Nino Sable, who released his first album in 2010 and has added several more albums to his discography over the years. The artist, who was born in Porto (Portugal) but is based in the Ruhr region (Germany), returned this year after an eight-year silence with his fourth album, consisting of fourteen songs. His musical universe lies somewhere between Chanson, Neo-Folk, and Balladry. The sound is primarily characterized by melancholy, which is transformed into beautiful, compelling songs, some of whose choruses are surprisingly catchy. A few synth sounds add an extra layer of melancholic atmosphere. The songs have a dreamy quality, yet remain consistently wistful. His deep, warm, and fitting voice is perfectly suited to the overall sound, with the acoustic guitar predominating throughout. This is an album full of depth and emotion that completely convinced me and will undoubtedly appeal to fans of Rome. As far as I am concerned, it is a beautiful discovery. (Rating:8). Sable recorded, produced, mixed and mastered the album himself in Essen between October 2025 and March 2026, playing all instruments and singing all vocals. Benno Schlicht added clarinet to “We Are Only Human”, and Sable also handled the artwork. Side-Line reported the release on the day it appeared, on 15 May 2026: Melanculia return with Nino Sable album ‘post mortem’. Listen to “The Tower”: The Tower by Melanculia About Melanculia Melanculia is the solo project of Nino Sable, born in Porto, Portugal, and based in Essen, in the German Ruhr region. Sable writes, performs and produces the material himself, mixing indie and alternative rock with slowcore and dream-pop, with acoustic guitar at the centre of the arrangements. The debut album “The Dazed Prophet” appeared on 18 October 2010, followed by “Paths” on 3 May 2013 and “Seventh Circle” on 10 December 2018. An eight-year gap separates that record from “Post Mortem”, the fourth Melanculia album, which was issued on 15 May 2026 and runs to fourteen tracks across roughly sixty-one minutes.
items._cn_summary: Melanculia 是葡萄牙裔音乐人 Nino Sable 的个人计划，2026年发行的第四张专辑《Post Mortem》收录十四首作品，时长约六十一分钟。整张专辑由 Sable 本人在德国埃森独立完成录音、制作、混音及母带处理，演奏全部乐器并演唱所有声部，仅有一首曲目邀请客座乐手演奏单簧管。音乐以原声吉他为骨架，融合香颂、新民谣与慢核的抒情质感，深沉温暖的嗓音贯穿始终，合成器音色为整体增添一层梦幻而忧郁的氛围。评论将其与同属悲怆美学脉络的 Rome 相提并论，认为旋律副歌部分出人意料地具有抓耳效果。这是一张情感浓度较高的独立制作专辑，在私密的内省气质与精致的编曲之间取得平衡。

items.body:
The legend behind Eurobeat anthem ‘Pump Up The Jam’ does folk and goth-pop in a fairly corny delivery from Stroom

After cropping up on a compilation EP (STREP-039) last year with the brooding balm of ‘Ambient Kinsky’, Jo Bogaert aka Thomas De Quincey (and tonnes more monikers) ‘fesses up to these languid and pretty cheesy cuts dating to his early years, spanning the Lemmiwinks-like strums and vox of ‘I Want You To Know Me’ and the prog-folk of ‘I Hear A Whale Song’ as part of White Light alongside Johan Guns, Kris Michiels, and Toon Vantilborgh, while the other two come from his 1983 solo album ‘None Of Them Are Green’, and follow his nose for black clad goth-rock and pop strums, including the vinegary strokes of ‘So Obscene.’
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了Jo Bogaert（又名Thomas De Quincey，曾以多组化名发行作品）在早年创作的两组曲目。White Light部分是与Johan Guns、Kris Michiels和Toon Vantilborgh合作完成的，呈现出轻柔的原声吉他拨奏与人声交织，并融入带有前卫摇滚色彩的鲸歌主题曲目；其余两首选自1983年个人专辑，展现了黑衫哥特摇滚与流行拨弦的阴郁面貌。整体氛围偏暖昧与怀旧，制作带有八十年代DIY气质，但旋律走向与编配被评价为略带俗套。评论将这张作品视为作者早期档案的一次集中披露，而非面向新听众的正式专辑企划。

items.body:
Michael J. Blood lends two rugged, tumping takes to Intertoto’s rudely groggy beatdown house

‘If I Take You Home’ is the first cut from London’s Intertoto since his well received album ‘Thermal Shadow’ (2023) and continues down a midnight path of mid-tempo, strutting beatdown roughly guided by likes of NWAQ and Kassel Mosse.

MJB steps it up a gear or two in a ‘Walk of Shame Mix’ built from woodcut kicks and gritty sampler revs plus additional vox like Martin Rev just walked in the room and did a Travolta “huh?”, plus a banging ‘Morning After Mix’ cloaked in muffled party noise and prompting jelly legs back to the ‘floor.
items._genre: beatdown house / mid-tempo electronic / dub-inflected house
items._cn_summary: 这是伦敦电子音乐人Intertoto在2023年专辑《Thermal Shadow》之后的首支新作，携手Michael J. Blood推出两个混音版本。原始版本以中速律动为核心，走午夜时分的暗调路线，木刻般的底鼓与粗砺的采样引擎声构成骨架，搭配的人声采样带有Martin Rev式的冷峻疏离感。'Walk of Shame Mix'进一步加重打击密度，'Morning After Mix'则裹挟在闷哑的派对噪音之中，呼应宿醉后摇摆归途的意象。整体制作偏向俱乐部场景的beatdown house领域，借鉴了NWAQ与Kassel Mosse的处理手法，音色粗粝但不失律动感。

items.body:
More slick sophisti-pop from the CPH scene via GB aka Gustav Berntsen, kinda heavily reminds us of a Japanoise/ jazz fusion take on Sam Prekop’s self-titled alltimer with bits of Red House Painters, Steely Dan and Prefab Sprout in there too.

Berntsen was stationed in London when he was writing 'Herzprung' and began to collect copies of the infamous free rag Metro, that he cut to shreds to fix up the lyrical portion of the songs. Once he had this in check, the Danish singer-songwriter called up his most trusted collaborators and booked a week at a studio "in the Swedish wilderness", where he dubbed the songs live to 24-track tape, encouraging improvisation and collaboration. And there's certainly a knottiness to this material that's unique to Bernsten; like many contemporary Copenhagen-based operatives, he's clearly well versed in classic rock and pop, from Fleetwood Mac and Steely Dan to Chick Corea and Haruomi Hosono, but he doesn't stop at pastiche, instead bringing his own absurdities to the table. "The Simpson's Season Six," he calls out harmoniously on opener 'Adrenaline', interrupting a stop-start drum fill and riffs that wouldn't sound out of place on a Gastr del Sol record. 

It would be hard to label 'Herzprung' post-rock, but there's a sense that Berntsen has at least learned from the genre's Chicago-era excesses. He seems to be driven by a holistic understanding of pop; at their heart, his songs are impeccably written, yet he's also not interested in taking the clearest path. On 'Belly', his cool-headed harmonies and almost tropicalia-strength choruses are complicated by winding instrumental sections and a phenomenally atmospheric dip into tape-fuckt cosmic ambience, while the lengthy 'Shit River' is a slowcore anthem that Berntsen expands with a full choir and an arsenal of synths.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由哥本哈根音乐人Gustav Berntsen在伦敦创作期间完成，他将免费小报Metro裁剪拼贴作为歌词素材，随后召集合作者在瑞典荒野的录音棚中以24轨磁带同期录制完成。整体风格融合了Steely Dan式的精致和声、Chick Corea与细野晴臣的爵士元素，并融入Gastr del Sol影响的器乐段落与磁带实验氛围。作品在流行框架内加入不规则的器乐展开、tape-fuckt宇宙氛围段落，以及慢核史诗式的合唱编制，试图在琅琅上口的旋律与复杂的结构之间寻找平衡。这种兼具旋律可听性与实验野心的做法使其偏向跨界融合领域，但对纯实验或前卫口味的听众而言可能仍显温和。

items.excerpt: 現代ルーツ・レゲエ界屈指のバンドによる5作目。中心人物であるセネガル生まれのメタ・ディアは影響を公言するボブ・マーリーから継承したような声質や歌い口だが、一音一音を丹念に歌いこむソウルフルな歌唱は、デニス・ブラウンや初期アスワド、ケン・ブースを思わせたりも。とりわけ中盤以降、その歌唱は水が紙に染み広がるように形を変え静かにレゲエの枠を拡張していく。サウンド面ではこれまで以上に1980年前後のルーツ・レゲエを尊重しつつ、ブルースやソウルからアフロR&Bまでをナチュラルに融合。懐古主義に終わらず、レゲエとアフリカの結び付きを現代の感性で照らし直した、ルーツ・レゲエの発展形と呼ぶに相応しい1枚となっている。

items._cn_summary: 塞内加尔出身的Meta Dia领衔的乐队带来第五张专辑，延续Bob Marley、Dennis Brown、Aswad一脉的Roots Reggae传统，但通过融入布鲁斯、灵魂乐与非洲节奏元素，将这一类型推向新的边界。主唱以灵魂深处的唱腔著称，歌声如同水浸纸张般逐渐扩散，悄然扩展雷鬼的框架。专辑在向1980年前后的Roots Reggae致敬的同时，不流于怀旧，而是以当代视角重新审视雷鬼与非洲的血脉联系。融合手法自然不生硬，涵盖了从蓝调到Afro R&B的多种色彩，是Roots Reggae发展形态的一次完整呈现。

items.body: On Reaching Ends, Part Timer (John McCaffrey) presents listeners with a collection of nine reflective songs. Running in at just over half an hour, it’s perfect downtime music. The instrumentals contain post-rock signatures, but they lean towards the ambient spectrum. Hints of experimentation hide within, too, with paper-creased lullabies and the lightest addition of playful, bright-eyed electronics. The guitar provides a selection of sleepy, late-afternoon melodies, which are permanently bright in tone. Nothing is out of place or overstays its welcome; everything has been trimmed to near-perfection, and it just feels right. Despite many of its songs coming in at a standard three minutes, there’s plenty of room for the music to expand, and they never feel dimmed in spite of the slim cut. Brevity allows the song to brightly shine. Each song is distinct, fully-fleshed, and mature, harbouring a unique personality while sharing a commonality in the kindness of its soul. McCaffrey is extremely talented when it comes to providing an accurate emotional picture and the state of the music’s current mood. His instrumentals are capable of saying more than vocal, lyric-based music. The songs gleam and radiate with their own spirit-warmth in spite of (or because of) its compressed lifespan. The title track is a drop-dead gorgeous knockout. In this song, the stirring string arrangements feel slim, despite their many numbers. Notes drip from the strings of the guitar, too, and all of the pieces fall into place naturally. At just over two minutes, it says enough, does enough, and even goes beyond, saying more in the space of two minutes than many say in ten. The lengthier ‘Final Form’ is beautiful and tender, as young and as a fresh as an infant. In this song, the splayed piano is joined by a light percussion – barely a brush against the sides of its soft piano – and the whole track feels like precious cargo; it contains a moment that can never be captured again, but one that remains in the heart forever, never dying or seeing decay. The perfect mixture of piano and strings, while also adding a gently-smudged background of ambient air, sees the music through. It’s reassuring, soft, and, above all, a slice of kindness. www.analoguechat1.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: 《Reaching Ends》是Part Timer（John McCaffrey）的一张器乐专辑，包含九首沉思性曲目，总长约半小时。作品带有后摇的特征，但明显倾向于氛围光谱，内部藏有实验性元素——纸褶般的摇篮曲片段、明亮俏皮的电子音色轻触其间。吉他提供慵懒的午后旋律，音色始终透亮。McCaffrey善于用器乐表达精确的情感画面，其音乐承载的信息量超过许多带歌词的作品。标题曲以弦乐编排为核心，吉他音符滴落自然，配合恰到好处；《Final Form》则以散开的钢琴与轻触鼓刷的打击乐结合，辅以微妙的氛围空气层，整体柔嫩如新生。专辑在剪辑上近乎完美，每首歌都拥有独立的个性与共同的灵魂温度。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

Bruce was, of course, a former member of Cream (with guitarist Eric Clapton and drummer Ginger Baker), Manfred Mann, John Mayall's Bluesbreakers (with Eric Clapton), and both the Graham Bond Organization (with Baker and Heckstall-Smith) and Graham Bond Quart
items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — The highly-revered bass player's first solo album release finds Jack supported in part by members of Colosseum (Dick Heckstall-Smith and Jon Hiseman), in part Nucleus (Chris Spedding and drummer John Marshall). Bruce was, of course, a former member of Cream (with guitarist Eric Clapton and drummer Ginger Baker), Manfred Mann, John Mayall's Bluesbreakers (with Eric Clapton), and both the Graham Bond Organization (with Baker and Heckstall-Smith) and Graham Bond Quartet (with Baker and guitarist John McLaughlin) as well as Alexis Korner's Blues Incorporated (his first collaboration with Baker and Heckstall-Smith). The material that became Songs for a Tailor was recorded in London in April and May of 1969 and then released in Britain by Polydor Records on August 29 of 1969 (Oct. 6 in the States by ATCO). 1. "Never Tell Your Mother She's Out of Tune" (3:41) R&B Brass Rock with a complex syncopated construction that uses dissonant chords from both the horn section as well as an unusual progression for the odd vocal melody to sing over. The drumming is particularly tight but it's the horn arrangements that really knock your socks off. Jack's bass playing is impressive, especially toward the end when he starts to stray outside the main riff he created to found the song over. Not a great nor memorable song except for the unusual horn arrangements. (8.875/10)2. "Theme for an Imaginary Western" (3:30) sounding like a PROCOL HARUM song with both vocal melody, band's chord progression, organ and piano dominance, and pace, Jack's voice has a kind of jazzy VAN MORRISON quality and styling to it. Another okay song. (8.75/10)3. "Tickets to Water Falls" (3:00) a brief piano intro turns into another unusual jazzy song with a bit of a Caribbean flavor to it despite its loud free-flowing Jazz-Rock bass and multiple keyboards and spicy rhythm guitar (which Chris Spedding later turns into a bit of a George Harrison-like solo). Very interesting. (8.875/10)4. "Weird of Hermiston" (2:24) a Blues-Rock based song that again crosses into that area of music that is more commonly traversed by artists like Van Morrison, The Band, Jethro Tull, and George Harrison--this might even be considered proto-Americana! (8.75/10)5. "Rope Ladder to the Moon" (2:54) a Blues-Rock song that sounds very much like it could have come from one of JETHRO TULL's earliest albums. I like this one. Even the vocal sounds as quirky and adventurous as something Ian Anderson (or Van Morrison) would do. (8.875/10)6. "The Ministry of Bag" (2:49) this one is pure Memphis Blues--as if Booker T & The M.G.'s and The Memphis Horns are on board from start to finish. Jack's singing is aggressive and bluesy like young Dr. John or Wilson Pickett. A top three song. (9/10)7. "He the Richmond" (3:36) Jack's strumming acoustic guitar opens this where he is joined by John Marshall's drums and his own bass while singing a vocal as if channelling a combination of Richie Havens, Ian Anderson, and Dr. John. The uncredited harmonizing vocals of the second minute are really unusual--and cool! A top three song for me. (9/10)8. "Boston Ball Game 1967" (1:45) loud horns and pounding piano dominate this one so much that Jack's multiple vocal(s) tracks are nearly drowned out (and seem to have to force themselves to be heard). Kind of cool but could've been turned into something more. (Or else.) (4.375/5)9. "To Isengard" (5:28) acoustic guitars strumming and picking while multiple vocal lines are tracking--the lead using a delicate, high-pitched timbre (that sounds like Rod Stewart trying to sing up high). Very interesting. I really like the vocal harmonies as well as the interplay between Jack and Chris' two guitars. At 3:15 there is a brief stop out of which explodes a uptempo motif that spreads things out among bass, drums, and the psychedelic sound creations and play of Chris Spedding's electric guitar. While I prefer the first half, I did enjoy the second half, too. My final top three song. (8.875/10)10. "The Clearout" (2:35) trying to go back to the Cream world? Heavy power chords from both electric guitar and bass over Jon Hiseman's Ginger Baker-like militaristic drumming. Not my favorite use of these talented artist's skills. And I didn't even mention the Roger Daltry-like singing or lyrics over the Beatles' "Birthday"-like melody line. (8.75/10)Total time 31:42Jack can certainly impress with his bass playing--as if he could be the father of Jaco Pastorius--but his active and jazzy lines (and sound) are not always as fitting to the music and his vocal stylings and lyrics aren't quite the kind of stuff for the AM charts. B/four stars; while I definitely appreciate the uniqueness of Jack's talents and vision, I find most of the music on this album to be almost confusing and messy, and the lyrics to be nearly impregnable and, probably, written from a very personal, albeit creative perspective (not unlike those of Van Morrison).
items._cn_summary: 这张1969年的专辑是贝斯手Jack Bruce的首张个人作品，参与乐手横跨Colosseum、Nucleus等乐队。整体以爵士摇滚与蓝调摇滚为底色，部分曲目融入RBRass Rock、加勒比律动，甚至被乐评人形容为'proto-Americana'的雏形。曲目大多短小精悍，编曲注重铜管组的非常规和声进行与切分节奏，贝斯线条倾向于在主riff之外自由游走。人声风格被比作Van Morrison与Ian Anderson的混合体，蓝调段落则有Memphis Blues的影子。虽然制作在当时具有一定先锋性，但以当代实验、前卫、爵士即兴的标尺衡量，其结构仍偏向传统歌曲形式，融合深度与声响探索有限。对偏好实验与即兴的听众而言，这张专辑更接近爵士摇滚史的入门文本，而非真正的创新前沿。

items.body: Twenty-five years is enough time for a cult film to acquire the patina of a period piece, but Gypsy 83 has always been preoccupied with people who regard the present tense as something to survive. Todd Stephens’s 2001 road trip movie follows two goth outsiders in Sandusky, Ohio: Gypsy Vale, played by Sara Rue, and her younger friend Clive Webb, played by Birkett Turton, whose devotion to Stevie Nicks offers both an aesthetic vocabulary and a plausible escape route. When they hear about New York City’s Night of 1000 Stevies, they climb into a car and head east, hoping that Gypsy might finally step onto a stage large enough for the person she imagines becoming. This month, the film is heading back to theaters in a considerably updated form. Gypsy 83: The Director’s Cut has been restored in 4K from the original 35mm camera negative and expanded to 138 minutes, compared with the 95-minute version released in 2001. More than forty minutes of previously unseen material have been restored, along with nine additional music tracks. The new edition opened at New York’s Quad Cinema on August 14 and begins a Los Angeles engagement at the Nuart Theatre on August 21, with additional screenings scheduled around the United States through September. For a movie so steeped in black clothes, pale faces, record collections, and the private language of fandom, Gypsy 83 has a surprisingly capacious heart. Gypsy and Clive are bonded by the sense that the lives available to them in Sandusky have already been written by other people. Their trip to Manhattan gives the film its engine, though Stephens is equally interested in the smaller humiliations and revelations that accumulate along the highway, where the pair encounter strangers whose desires prove no simpler than their own. The legendary Karen Black appears as Bambi LeBleau, a faded lounge singer whose theatricality gives the travelers a glimpse of adulthood as both performance and improvisation. John Doe, of X, plays Gypsy’s father, Ray, while Paulo Costanzo and Anson Scoville round out a cast populated by characters who seem to exist just beyond the borders of respectable small-town life. The film places goth culture within an American road-movie tradition usually reserved for cowboys, drifters, runaways, and seekers, allowing eyeliner, Stevie Nicks devotion, queer longing, and friendship to occupy the passenger seat without requiring translation. The film also occupies a central place in Stephens’s career. After writing and producing the 1998 coming-of-age film Edge of Seventeen, he made his directorial debut with Gypsy 83. Those two films, followed two decades later by Swan Song, form the Ohio trilogy through which Stephens has repeatedly returned to Sandusky, his hometown, as a setting for queer lives formed within the constraints of a Midwestern city. Stephens and editor Anderson Matthew recut the picture from scratch, a process that ultimately stretched across several years. Stephens has said that locating the original negative required detective work after the New York laboratory that had stored it went out of business; the material was eventually traced to a vault in California. The recovered 35mm elements became the basis for the new 4K restoration. Music, always central to the film’s conception of identity, has also been given more room. The restored soundtrack draws on The Cure, Cocteau Twins, Echo & the Bunnymen, Switchblade Symphony, Ministry, Alien Sex Fiend, and Clan of Xymox, alongside Diva Destruction’s cover of “Talk to Me” and Nobody’s Wolf Child’s rendition of “Song to the Siren.” The added material changes more than the running time: songs that once functioned as cultural shorthand can now inhabit scenes at greater length, giving the characters more space to live inside the music that helped them invent themselves Altered Innocence is handling the new theatrical release. After its August 14–20 run at Quad Cinema, the film plays Los Angeles from August 21–27, followed by Seattle on August 26 and 27, San Francisco on August 27, Houston on August 29, Nashville on August 31, Philadelphia on September 3, and Denver on September 11. A home-video release is planned for later this year. A quarter-century after Gypsy and Clive first pointed their car toward Manhattan, their destination may be the least interesting part of the trip. What has endured is the film’s understanding of subculture as a form of shelter: the clothes, songs, heroes, jokes, and gestures through which isolated people recognize one another before they have found a more permanent place to belong. The Director’s Cut returns to that idea with forty additional minutes and the advantage of time, allowing Stephens to revisit a film that once left him wounded and finally present the version he had been carrying with him all along. In US cinemas now. Full dates and tickets can be found here. Blu-ray and streaming will follow in November 2026. items.body: Berlin art-pop and indietronica artist Gene Sophia Bogolepov release “Slow Down Your Burning” on 3 September 2026 through MYCELM, the label and archive Bogolepov run from the same city. It is the first single from “Dråma”, a nine-track album set for 11 November 2026, and it carries the darkwave and experimental edges that have run through the project since its move to Germany. The album will be sold through Bandcamp, Qobuz and the MYCELM platform. It will not appear on Spotify in full. MYCELM states that the omission follows the artist’s ideological beliefs, so the album is being kept off the largest streaming service by choice rather than by a licensing gap. “Dråma” was assembled by a small group. Diego Ferri handled guitars, production and engineering, Volodymyr Nestryga played drums and percussion, Dimitri Klochkov contributed guitars, bass and synths, and Scout Hansen co-wrote. Piano parts came from Andrian Lebedev, who died in 2021. How ‘Dråma’ began, four days before the invasion On 20 February 2022, four days before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Bogolepov was in the studio with Scout Hansen, working while anxious about what was coming. “Serpent Song” came out of that session, written from inside the mind of a psychopath, and the rest of the album grew around it over the four years that followed. MYCELM describes the result as “an album about faith, justice, violence, and what happens when catastrophe becomes ordinary.” The 2017 song “Mother Russia” drew enough hostility in Russia to push the artist into exile, and the move to Berlin reset the project. “Art Brut” followed in 2021. Onstage the current line-up is a duo: Bogolepov with Diego Ferri, a Berlin musician and sound engineer who played guitar for and produced the Canadian lo-fi act Michelle Gurevich, and whose other credits take in BBC1 and work with Martin Bisi, the New York producer behind records by Sonic Youth and Swans. Recent appearances include Ms Artville Festival in Hamburg in 2021, Noorderzon Festival in Groningen and WORM in Rotterdam in 2022, Berghain in 2024 and LARK in Berlin in 2025. MYCELM has also submitted the album to Wave-Gotik-Treffen 2027. No 2027 WGT line-up has been announced, so no booking is confirmed. About Gene Sophia Bogolepov Gene Sophia Bogolepov grew up in a working-class household in Saint Petersburg, surrounded by family instruments, and first performed in 2003. The early electropunk project T-Lazarus came out of that period, followed by the electro-rock band Gender ID, which played across Russia and Europe on bills with Ladytron, Placebo, Editors, Sparks and Apparat Band. Two further projects, Dukes of Betelgeuse and Ego Collider, ran alongside them. In 2013 Bogolepov adopted the name 1314 and turned the work towards living with HIV, anxiety and queer isolation. The 2017 anti-authoritarian song “Mother Russia” produced a backlash that led to exile, and Berlin became the base from then on. “Art Brut” arrived in 2021, and the catalogue collected on the MYCELM platform now runs from “Ultrawhite” and “Home Kids & Bathroom Romance” through “[bodies] EP”, “Deviant Comedy”, the 1314 LP, “Art Brut”, “Long Awaited Silence Of Mind (坂本龍一に捧げる)”, the “Titanium” EP and the “Art Brut (Mycelium Edition)” reissue. MYCELM itself began as Mycelium, a paywalled discography archive, and relaunched under its current name in February 2026 as what Bogolepov describes as an archive, community and label for underground and unsigned artists, most of them queer. It publishes as Mycelm Records and Mycelm Publishing out of Berlin, and it now handles both “Slow Down Your Burning” and “Dråma”.
items._cn_summary: 柏林艺术家Gene Sophia Bogolepov即将通过自营厂牌MYCELM发行专辑《Dråma》，首支单曲《Slow Down Your Burning》定于2026年9月释出。专辑包含九首曲目，录制团队规模精简，由Diego Ferri主导制作与吉他，融合暗潮与实验电子元素。创作起点可追溯至2022年2月俄乌冲突前夕，作品围绕信仰、正义、暴力及灾难常态化等主题展开。钢琴部分由已故的Andrian Lebedev录制。艺术家早年因反权威立场被迫流亡，2013年起以HIV、焦虑与酷儿孤绝为创作核心。专辑拒绝上架Spotify，仅在Bandcamp、Qobuz及MYCELM平台发行，附带明确的意识形态立场。该文属于新闻通稿性质，聚焦发行信息与背景介绍，对音乐本身的音响特征与艺术价值鲜有实质评论，信息量有限。

items.album: NCN 19: Nik Kershaw, Die Krupps, SKYND, Diary of Dreams and more head to Deutzen
